body:
# v1.33.5 (Patch Release)

<!-- alex-c-line-start-release-status -->
**Status**: Released
<!-- alex-c-line-end-release-status -->

<!-- alex-c-line-start-release-summary -->
This is a new patch release of the `alex-c-line` package. It fixes issues with the package and should require no refactoring. Please read the description of changes below.
<!-- alex-c-line-end-release-summary -->

## Description of Changes

- When writing the global cache file, add a new line to the end of the file.
    - I am picky.
    - I know we almost never look into the cache file directly, but it just bothers me not to have it there anyway.

## Additional Notes - v2 Preparation

- Just a heads up - I am going to pause ALL new features for `alex-c-line` until v2 comes out from this point on.
- The only time a new feature will be added is if it is needed in an emergency case to unblock something else (e.g. I needed the internal commands I added recently to unblock dependency updates).
- `alex-c-line` needs quite a bit cleanup as of now as it has quite a lot of legacy features still present that can make it harder to design new features around.
- I am aiming to release v2 by mid-March, and no later than the end of the month.
- This will give me a chance to control the surface area and really decide what we want to carry forward and continue supporting, and what really is just legacy and can be removed in favour of newer and better features.
- Fundamental changes to come include:
    - Consolidation of the dynamic config system (both private and public configs)
    - The caching system
    - Use of subcommands rather than the pure flat commands we have been using up to this point.
    - Removing deprecated features and tightening command names.
- With this new direction, I'm hoping to take `alex-c-line` from just another package that can be installed into a project into essentially its own mini-app that can be used anywhere you can use a terminal.
- Not only will it continue helping with my own tooling and infrastructure, it'll also have more project-agnostic commands that can improve the developer experience even in repositories that don't yet have `alex-c-line`.
- With all that said, keep an eye out on this space for more information!






















- ...did I really just add a new line to the cache just so I can make this announcement?
- The answer is no - I did actually want to fix that. Again, I am picky!
- Lack of ending new line in a file? Yeah, that's absolutely an emergency case right there, obviously!

author: notcome
body:
## Summary

Add workspace root as a context source for both skills and AGENTS.md files, sitting between user-level (`~/.wuhu/`) and project-level (environment root) in the override hierarchy.

## Changes

### 1. Configurable workspace path

Added `workspacePath` to `WuhuServerConfig` with a `resolveWorkspaceRoot(databasePath:)` helper. When set, the config value (tilde-expanded) is used. Otherwise falls back to `<dataRoot>/workspace` (existing behavior).

Refactored `WuhuWorkspaceDocsStore` to accept `workspaceRoot:` directly instead of deriving it from `dataRoot`.

### 2. Workspace skills loading

Skills loading order (later overrides earlier by name):
1. **User**: `~/.wuhu/skills/`
2. **Workspace**: `<workspaceRoot>/skills/`
3. **Project**: `<envRoot>/.wuhu/skills/`

Workspace skills have source `"workspace"`.

### 3. Workspace AGENTS.md loading

AGENTS.md loading order (all included, broadest scope first):
1. **Workspace**: `<workspaceRoot>/AGENTS.md`
2. **Environment root**: `<envRoot>/AGENTS.md`
3. **Session CWD**: `<cwd>/AGENTS.md`

(Plus `AGENTS.local.md` variants at each level.)

Duplicate paths are deduplicated, so when cwd == envRoot the file appears only once.

Fixed a pre-existing issue where AGENTS.md files were sorted alphabetically by path, destroying the intentional scope ordering.

### Plumbing

`workspaceRoot` is threaded through:
- `WuhuServer` → `WuhuService` → `SQLiteSessionStore.createSession` (for skills)
- `WuhuService` → `WuhuSessionRuntime.setContextCwd` → `WuhuAgentsContextActor` (for AGENTS.md)
- `WuhuService` → `forkCodingSession` / `createDirectSession` (for child sessions)

## Tests

- 131 tests pass (7 new)
- Config: `loadsWorkspacePath`, `resolveWorkspaceRootUsesConfigWhenSet`, `resolveWorkspaceRootFallsBackToDataRoot`
- Skills: `createSessionLoadsSkillsFromWorkspaceRoot`, `projectSkillOverridesWorkspaceSkillWithSameName`
- AGENTS.md: `loadsAgentsFromWorkspaceAndEnvironmentRoots`, `deduplicatesAgentsWhenCwdEqualsEnvironmentRoot`

author: copilot
body:
AI (NPC) agents had no mechanism to influence division leader elections before they happen. This adds a `CampaignRoutine` that drives characters to canvass voters in public spaces and use PRAISE/DENOUNCE meeting agendas to shift mutuality — which directly determines vote distribution in `Party.getVotes()`.

## New: `CampaignRoutine`
- Moves to public places (`market`, `squareNorth`, `squareSouth`), preferring locations with uncontacted voters
- Initiates `AttendPrivateMeetingRoutine` talks with party members not yet approached (tracked in `triedTalkingTo`)
- In-meeting agenda selection:
  - **PRAISE** highest-mutuality candidate (self-promotion eligible if character is a director) when above `FriendMutualityThreshold`
  - **DENOUNCE** lowest-mutuality candidate when below `EnemyMutualityThreshold`
- Self-terminates when the election leaves `scheduledMeetings`

## Trigger: `WorkRoutine`
Characters in their own division campaign during work hours when `pScale + rScale > 1.5` or the `"charismatic"` trait is present.

## Trigger: `DowntimeRoutine`
Characters campaign during free time for any party they belong to when `pScale + extrovert bonus > 0.8`.

## How it closes the loop
```
CampaignRoutine → PRAISE/DENOUNCE agendas → mutuality shifts → Party.getVotes() picks winner
```
Votes are weighted by each member's mutuality toward candidates, so sustained campaigning materially affects election outcomes.

- New route file `maestro/api/routes/musehub/labels.py` implementing all 8 label endpoints
- Pydantic request/response models defined inline: `LabelCreate`, `LabelUpdate`, `LabelResponse`, `LabelListResponse`, `AssignLabelsRequest`

| Method | Path | Auth |
|--------|------|------|
| GET | `/api/v1/musehub/repos/{repo_id}/labels` | public |
| POST | `/api/v1/musehub/repos/{repo_id}/labels` | required |

author: abn
body:
In Flatpak (without --share=pid) and similar PID-namespace-isolated environments, getpgid() returns -1 for a live server process because the PID in the file is sandbox-internal and invisible to the caller. This caused the PID file to be deleted and status to falsely report the server as not running.

Add an HTTP liveness check (GET /api/version) before treating a negative getpgid() result as stale. If the server responds, the PID file is kept and the server is reported as running.

Also extract a shared http_server_alive() helper and apply both the pre-stale HTTP check and the lsof/pgrep port-based fallback to all Unix platforms — both tools are available on Linux and macOS, and the sandbox isolation concern is not Linux-exclusive.

author: srmanda-cs
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/srmanda-cs/terraform-provider-cloudlab/security/code-scanning/1](https://github.com/srmanda-cs/terraform-provider-cloudlab/security/code-scanning/1)

To fix the problem, explicitly restrict the `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions used by this workflow/job. Since the steps only check out code, set up Go, build, and run linting, they only need read access to the repository contents.

The best fix without changing functionality is to add a `permissions:` block with `contents: read`. You can add it at the workflow root (so it applies to all jobs) or at the job level. Because there is only one job in the shown snippet, adding it at the root is simplest and clearly documents the workflow’s needs.

Concretely, edit `.github/workflows/test.yml` to insert:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
```

between the `on:` block and the `jobs:` block. No imports or other definitions are needed.

author: jwilson02
body:
💡 **What**: Replaced `FileReader.readAsDataURL` with `URL.createObjectURL` for local image previews. Also added `useEffect` cleanup to release memory and prevent memory leaks. Added learning entry to `.jules/bolt.md`.

🎯 **Why**: Using `FileReader` to read files as base64 strings is memory intensive (since it loads the entire file string into memory) and can cause slight blocking on the main thread when generating previews for large images. `URL.createObjectURL` creates a fast, lightweight, synchronous reference directly to the local file without reading its contents.

📊 **Impact**: Faster image preview generation with reduced memory footprint, especially noticeable with large image files. Prevents main thread stuttering during file drops or selections.

🔬 **Measurement**: Verify by uploading a very large image file (e.g., > 10MB) via drag-and-drop or file selection. The UI should instantly display the preview without hanging or freezing.

author: jinboyan
body:
# SupaCloud Multi-tenant Infrastructure Improvements

This PR introduces critical fixes and architectural improvements for SupaCloud's multi-tenant environment, specifically targeting Edge Functions reliability, environment variable security/extensibility, and database connection stability under pooled environments.

## Core Changes

### 1. Edge Runtime: Dynamic Static Router Generation

**Problem**: Deno based Edge Runtime often fails with `Module not found` when using dynamic `import()` within the compilation sandbox, especially in persistent container environments.
**Solution**: Modified `function_manager.sh` to automatically generate a flattened `index.ts` entry point using **static imports** for all tenant functions before starting the runtime.

- **Benefit**: Ensures 100% reliability for function loading.
- **Implementation**: Functions are now deployed as `<slug>.ts` in a flattened structure, and the router is regenerated on every deploy or start.

### 2. Secure & Extensible Environment Injection

**Problem**: The previous `grep` logic was prone to partial matches (e.g., `JWT_SECRET` matching `PGRST_JWT_SECRET`) and lacked support for custom third-party credentials (like WeChat AppID).
**Solution**:

- Standardized `grep -E '^KEY='` for exact line matching.
- Added explicit support for `WECHAT_APP_ID` and `WECHAT_APP_SECRET`.
- Improved extraction logic to handle duplicated keys in `.env` files.

### 3. PgBouncer & Auth (GoTrue) Compatibility

**Problem**: GoTrue's DB migrator requires prepared statements, which are unsupported by PgBouncer in `transaction` mode.
**Solution**:

- **GoTrue**: Switched the storage/auth DB connection to the direct PostgreSQL port (`5432`) while keeping PostgREST on the pooled port (`6432`).
- **PostgREST**: Explicitly disabled prepared statements via `PGRST_DB_PREPARED_STATEMENTS=false` to ensure stability through the pooler.

### 4. API Gateway Routing Precision

**Problem**: Global `/functions/v1` routes were occasionally shadowing tenant-specific routes.
**Solution**: Standardized all function routes to use trailing slashes `/functions/v1/` and adjusted priority in `gateway_manager.sh`.

## Verification

Verified on a production-like Rocky Linux 9 environment with Angie:

- [x] Correct routing of tenant requests to isolated containers.
- [x] Successful execution of WeChat Login function with full secret access.
- [x] Stable GoTrue startup and migrations behind PgBouncer.

---
*Note: This PR consolidates fixes from real-world 404/400 debugging sessions in high-isolation multi-tenant scenarios.*

author: copilot
body:
ES modules are always deferred — they run *after* regular scripts. `main.js` imports THREE as an ES module but never sets `window.THREE`, so `camp-world.js`, `blood-system.js`, and `spawn-sequence.js` (all regular scripts) find `THREE` undefined at execution time, crash silently, and leave critical globals like `window.CampWorld` unset. `loading.js` then times out after 60 seconds with "Game engine failed to start".

## Changes

- **`js/three-bridge.js`** (new): ES module that imports THREE via the import map, assigns `window.THREE = THREE`, then dynamically and sequentially loads the three dependent scripts so they execute only after `window.THREE` is set:
  ```javascript
  import * as THREE from 'three';
  window.THREE = THREE;
  // loads blood-system.js → spawn-sequence.js → camp-world.js in order
  ```

- **`index.html`**: Adds `<script type="module" src="js/three-bridge.js"></script>` immediately after the import map; removes the three static `<script>` tags for `blood-system.js`, `spawn-sequence.js`, and `camp-world.js` (now owned by the bridge).

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## The REAL root cause: window.THREE is never set, so camp-world.js and blood-system.js crash silently

### The Problem Chain

1. **`index.html` line 694-701** defines an import map for THREE.js:
   ```html
   <script type="importmap">
     { "imports": { "three": "https://unpkg.com/three@0.176.0/build/three.module.js" } }
   </script>
   ```

2. **`js/camp-world.js` (line 725, regular script, 94KB)** expects `THREE` to be available via `window.THREE`:
   ```javascript
   // Architecture: Regular script (not ES-module) – THREE via window.THREE
   ```
   It uses `THREE.Scene()`, `THREE.BoxGeometry()`, `THREE.MeshStandardMaterial()`, etc. directly.

3. **`js/blood-system.js` (line 723, regular script)** also uses `window.THREE`:
   ```javascript
   _geo = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
   _mat = new THREE.PointsMaterial({...});
   _points = new THREE.Points(_geo, _mat);
   ```

4. **`js/main.js` (line 749, ES module)** does `import * as THREE from 'three'` but **NEVER sets `window.THREE = THREE`**.

5. Since `camp-world.js` runs BEFORE `main.js` (it's a regular script at line 725, main.js is a module at line 749), `window.THREE` is undefined when camp-world.js executes → **camp-world.js crashes silently** → `window.CampWorld` is never created.

6. When `main.js` finally runs, it tries to use `window.CampWorld` which doesn't exist → things break → `window.setGamePaused` and `window.updateCampScreen` may never get set.

7. `loading.js` polls for these globals, never finds them after 60 seconds → shows "Game engine failed to start".

### The Fix — Add a THREE.js bridge script

We need TWO changes:

#### 1. Create a new file: `js/three-bridge.js`

This tiny script dynamically imports THREE.js using the import map and sets `window.THREE`:

```javascript
// three-bridge.js — Exposes THREE on window for regular (non-module) scripts
// Must be loaded as type="module" BEFORE camp-world.js, blood-system.js, etc.
// Uses the import map defined in index.html to resolve 'three'.

import * as THREE from 'three';
window.THREE = THREE;
console.log('[three-bridge] THREE.js loaded and exposed on window.THREE');
```

#### 2. Modify `index.html` to load the bridge BEFORE helper scripts

Find this section (around line 710-728):
```html
  <!-- Debug/diagnostic layer (observation-only, gated by ?debug=1) -->
  <script src="js/debug.js"></script>

  <!-- Extracted game modules (regular scripts, must load before main.js module) -->
  <script src="js/state.js"></script>
```

And add the bridge script RIGHT BEFORE the extracted game modules:
```html
  <!-- Debug/diagnostic layer (observation-only, gated by ?debug=1) -->
  <script src="js/debug.js"></script>

  <!-- THREE.js bridge: load THREE via ES module import map and expose on window -->
  <!-- This MUST run before camp-world.js, blood-system.js, and other scripts that use window.THREE -->
  <script type="module" src="js/three-bridge.js"></script>

  <!-- Extracted game modules (regular scripts, must load before main.js module) -->
  <script src="js/state.js"></script>
```

### WAIT — There's a problem with this approach!

ES modules (`type="module"`) are **deferred** — they run AFTER all regular scripts. So even if we add `three-bridge.js` as a module before the regular scripts, it will still run AFTER them.

### The REAL fix — use a top-level await inline module

Instead of a separate file, add an **inline module script** with a blocking approach. Actually, the cleanest solution is:

#### Option A: Convert camp-world.js and blood-system.js to lazy-init pattern

Since we can't make `window.THREE` available synchronously before regular scripts, we need to make `camp-world.js` **wait** for `window.THREE` instead of using it immediately.

BUT camp-world.js is 94KB and we can't edit it reliably.

#### Option B (BEST): Add the bridge as an inline script that blocks

Add this inline module script in `index.html` right after the import map, BEFORE any other scripts:

In `index.html`, right after line 701 (`</script>` closing the importmap), add:

```html
  <!-- Load THREE.js and expose on window BEFORE any other scripts -->
  <script type="module">
    import * as THREE from 'three';
    window.THREE = THREE;
    window.dispatchEvent(new Event('three-ready'));
  </script>
```

But wait — this is still deferred. ES modules always run after regular scripts.

#### Option C (ACTUALLY WORKS): Wrap helper scripts to wait for THREE

The real solution: the helper scripts (camp-world.js, blood-system.js) that need `window.THREE` should be loaded AFTER THREE is available. We can do this by:

1. Creating `js/three-bridge.js` as a module that imports THREE and sets window.THREE
2. In `index.html`, change the helper scripts that need THREE to be loaded dynamically AFTER the bridge

Actually the simplest approach that WILL work:

### SIMPLEST FIX THAT WORKS:

Create `js/three-bridge.js`:
```javascript
import * as THREE from 'three';
window.THREE = THREE;

// Now dynamically load all scripts that depen...

</details>

author: priyanka-kukreja
body:
## Summary
- Extract `ids` from `kwargs` before passing to `add_texts`/`aadd_texts` to prevent `TypeError: got multiple values for keyword argument 'ids'`
- Add regression tests for both sync and async methods

Fixes #32283

## Problem
When calling `add_documents` or `aadd_documents` with explicit `ids`:
```python
await vector_store.aadd_documents(documents, ids=["doc_1", "doc_2"])
```

The `ids` parameter was passed both:
1. Inside `**kwargs` (as `kwargs["ids"]`)
2. And then unpacked via `**kwargs` to `aadd_texts`

This caused Python to raise:
```
TypeError: aadd_texts() got multiple values for keyword argument 'ids'
```

## Solution
Extract `ids` from `kwargs` using `pop()` before calling `add_texts`/`aadd_texts`, then pass it explicitly:
```python
ids = kwargs.pop("ids", None)
return self.add_texts(texts, metadatas, ids=ids, **kwargs)
```

## Test plan
- [x] Added `test_add_documents_with_explicit_ids_no_duplicate_error` - sync regression test
- [x] Added `test_aadd_documents_with_explicit_ids_no_duplicate_error` - async regression test
- [x] Added `test_aadd_documents_without_ids_still_works` - ensures fix doesn't break normal usage
- [x] All 15 vectorstore tests pass

author: marcus
body:
## Problem

When sidecar is started from a **subfolder** of a git repo (e.g. `cd myrepo/src && sidecar`), `WorkDir` is set to that subfolder. Both `doCreateWorktree` (worktree.go) and `fetchAndCreateWorktree` (fetch_pr.go) computed the new worktree's parent as `filepath.Dir(WorkDir)`, which resolves to the **git root itself** — placing the new worktree *inside* the main repo instead of beside it.

This caused `git worktree add` to fail with `fatal: invalid reference: <branch>: exit status 128` because the path conflicted with existing repo contents.

## Fix

Use `ProjectRoot` (already correctly resolved to the main worktree path via `GetMainWorktreePath` in main.go) as the anchor for the parent-dir calculation. Falls back to `WorkDir` if `ProjectRoot` is empty.

**Before (broken when started from subfolder):**
```
WorkDir   = /repos/myrepo/subfolder
parentDir = /repos/myrepo        ← git root, not its parent!
wtPath    = /repos/myrepo/feat   ← INSIDE the main repo
```

**After (fixed):**
```
ProjectRoot = /repos/myrepo
parentDir   = /repos             ← parent of main repo ✓
wtPath      = /repos/feat        ← sibling of main repo ✓
```

## Testing

- All existing tests pass (`go test ./...`)
- Added `TestWorktreePathResolvesFromProjectRoot` regression test

Fixes #174

author: keks0r
body:
## Summary
Fixed backfill MV replay SQL generation to include an explicit column list in the INSERT clause. This prevents positional column mismatches when the materialized view uses `SELECT *` and adds computed columns.

## The Problem
When `INSERT INTO target SELECT ...` is used with a SELECT that expands `SELECT *` and appends computed columns, ClickHouse matches columns by position. If the SELECT output order doesn't match the target table's column order, ClickHouse attempts to insert incompatible types, causing errors like "Array(String) cannot be inside Nullable column".

## The Solution
Generate `INSERT INTO target (col1, col2, ...)` with an explicit column list from the target table's schema definition. This forces ClickHouse to match columns by name instead of position, matching the behavior of live materialized view inserts.

## Testing
- All 46 backfill plugin tests pass, including a new test verifying the explicit column list is generated correctly
- Added comprehensive test case covering the exact scenario described in the bug report

`loadTemplateFromString` in `pkg/authn/ui/ui.go` uses `text/template`, which does no output escaping. User-controlled values rendered through `{{ .Data.* }}` pass through raw into HTML responses. `html/template` is a drop-in replacement that auto-escapes by rendering context. 1. Import swap: `text/template` to `html/template`. All template types and FuncMap calls are in the `template` namespace already, nothing else changes. 2. `brsplitline`: escapes input with `HTMLEscapeString` before inserting `
` tags, returns `template.HTML` so the intentional tags aren't double-escaped. author: copilot
body:
Implements a runnable example combining QLoRA (4-bit quantization + LoRA) with DPO for preference-based fine-tuning, using only publicly available data and designed to work on local hardware (CPU or GPU).

## Changes

### `train_qlora_dpo.py`
- **Data**: Auto-downloads [`Anthropic/hh-rlhf`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Anthropic/hh-rlhf) from HuggingFace Hub; preprocesses into `{prompt, chosen, rejected}` format expected by `DPOTrainer`
- **QLoRA**: Loads `facebook/opt-125m` with `BitsAndBytesConfig` (NF4, double quantization, fp16 compute), then wraps with `LoraConfig` targeting `q_proj`/`v_proj`; falls back to fp32 on CPU automatically
- **DPO**: Trains via `trl.DPOTrainer` with configurable β; no PPO/reward model needed
- **Config**: All hyperparameters (model, dataset, LoRA rank, DPO β, sample limits, output dir) centralized in a `ScriptConfig` dataclass

```python
# Core QLoRA setup
bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(
    load_in_4bit=True,
    bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
    bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.float16,
    bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True,
)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name, quantization_config=bnb_config)
model = prepare_model_for_kbit_training(model)
model = get_peft_model(model, LoraConfig(r=16, target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"], ...))

# DPO training
trainer = DPOTrainer(model=model, args=DPOConfig(beta=0.1, ...), train_dataset=..., ...)
trainer.train()
```

### `requirements.txt`
Pins `torch`, `transformers`, `datasets`, `peft`, `trl`, `bitsandbytes`, `accelerate`, `scipy`.

### `README.md`
Documents setup, all config parameters, and the DPO loss formulation.

body:
This branch is intended to be the basis for the hledger 2.0 preview 1 discussed at https://github.com/simonmichael/hledger/issues/2547#issuecomment-3922324046 . I hope to release that soon, ideally with 1.52.

It mainly contains the automated lot tracking functionality I have been working on this month. This adds a major missing feature to hledger. It is working for me so far, but it's experimental and needs user testing and refinement. See also:

- #1015
- https://joyful.com/hledger+lot+tracking

and for background:

- [Tax Lot Accounting](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/t/taxlotaccounting.asp)
- [Tax Lot Accounting: A Comprehensive Guide for Investors](https://fastercapital.com/content/Tax-Lot-Accounting--A-Comprehensive-Guide-for-Investors.html)
- [IRS: Topic no. 409, Capital gains and losses](https://www.irs.gov/taxtopics/tc409)
- [IRS: About Publication 551, Basis of Assets]()


This also represents the first serious use of AI tools in the project. hledger 1.x was developed with no AI assistance; hledger 2.x will carefully explore AI-assisted development. Most of the new code in this branch was generated with claude code + sonnet/opus, guided by me. I have started an AI policy doc which will hopefully grow to answer common questions.

I have reviewed each commit myself, all tests are passing and many new ones were added, and I have done a fair amount of testing with my own journals. I would love any additional human review but wow that's a lot of commits, so I don't expect too much. If you have time please take a look at code, tests, docs, and/or build and try it out. This branch will be released as a preview and anything can be changed if needed.

AI policy:
- [doc/AI.md](https://github.com/simonmichael/hledger/blob/lots/doc/AI.md)

Lot tracking:
- Manual: [Basis / lots](https://github.com/simonmichael/hledger/blob/lots/hledger/hledger.m4.md#basis--lots), [Lot reporting](https://github.com/simonmichael/hledger/blob/lots/hledger/hledger.m4.md#lot-reporting)
- Example entries: [examples/lots/lot-entries.journal](https://github.com/simonmichael/hledger/blob/lots/examples/lots/lot-entries.journal)
- Tests: [hledger/test/journal/lots*](https://github.com/simonmichael/hledger/tree/lots/hledger/test/journal)
- Dev docs: [doc/{SPEC,PLAN,NOTE}*](https://github.com/simonmichael/hledger/tree/lots/doc)

A little more on this lot tracking design:

- It is obviously inspired by, learns from, and tries to be quite compatible with, the lot tracking in Ledger and (especially) Beancount.
- It is a hybrid of Ledger's/Beancount's amount-based cost basis annotations, and hledger 1.x's explicit lot subaccounts; both are supported. You can use whichever notation is more convenient in a given situation.
- It aims to be good at inferring missing information, so that often minimal or even no special notation is required. Existing journal entries might not need to change much.
- It also allows everything to be recorded explicitly, so that nothing is hidden and lot information can be passed to a new file or exported to another system.
- It aims to be pervasive: --lots mode makes detailed lots appear in all other reports, making it relatively easy to view and understand complex lot movements.
- It aims to be optional: when not using --lots mode, everything should work as it always has.
- It aims to support both global and per-account reduction methods, so that it can handle eg past and present US tax rules.
- AI use is in the air right now, but rustledger has been influential in demonstrating its effectiveness for PTA development.

body:
# ✅ SCRUM-57 – Token Cancellation UI

Branch: `feature/SCRUM-57-token-cancellation-ui`  
TypeScript check: ✅ 0 errors

---

## 📌 Overview

This PR implements the full **Token Cancellation UI flow**, fully integrated with the backend cancellation logic from SCRUM-55/56.

The UI now allows users to safely cancel tokens, handles all loading/error states properly, and refreshes queue data dynamically after cancellation.

---

## 📦 tokenApi.ts

### Changes
- Updated `UserToken` interface:
  - Added `cancelledAt: string | null`
- Added:

```ts
cancelToken(tokenId: number)
```

- Calls:

```http
PUT /api/Token/{id}/cancel
```

- Uses `extractErrorMessage` to properly pipe backend errors to UI
- Prevents generic JS error fallbacks

---

## 🎴 UserTokenCard.tsx

### New Prop

```ts
onCancel?: (tokenId: number) => Promise<void>
```

### Cancel Button Logic
- Visible only when:
  - `status === 'Waiting'`
  - `onCancel` is provided

### Safety & UX Improvements
- Two-step confirmation:
  - "Cancel this token?"
  - Options:
    - Yes, Cancel
    - Keep Token
- Prevents accidental taps

### Loading & Error Handling
- Spinner displayed during in-flight PUT request
- Cancel button disabled while loading
- Inline error message shown for:
  - Wrong owner
  - Not in `Waiting` status
  - Network/API failures

### Cancelled State UI
- Red banner displayed
- Shows exact `cancelledAt` timestamp
- Queue info panel hidden for cancelled tokens

### Status Styling
- Added `NoShow` to `getStatusColor`
- Purple status indicator

---

## 📊 DashboardPage.tsx

### Refactoring
- Extracted `fetchTokens` into `useCallback` for reuse

### New Handler

```ts
handleCancelToken(tokenId)
```

- Awaits:

```ts
tokenApi.cancelToken(tokenId)
```

- Calls `fetchTokens()` afterward to:
  - Refresh queue positions
  - Refresh ETA
  - Refresh statuses

### Component Wiring

```tsx
onCancel={handleCancelToken}
```

---

## 🚀 Final Outcome

- Full frontend cancellation integration
- Real-time queue refresh after cancellation
- Proper error propagation from backend
- Safe confirmation UX
- Clean TypeScript build (0 errors)

---

**Status:** Ready for review  
**Sprint:** SCRUM-57

author: copyleftdev
body:
## Summary
Fixes two confirmed issues from Deep Review 45: the `tools/list` response is now built once via `OnceLock` and reused across requests, and `send_message` now includes an `"indexed"` field so clients can detect when the Tantivy index operation was dropped.

## Changes
- `test: add 5 DR45 deep review tests (258 → 263)` — 5 hypothesis tests covering tools/list determinism, single-recipient clone path, triple registration identity stability, send response indexed field, and limit=1 partial drain.
- `fix: resolve DR45 confirmed issues (cached tools/list, indexed field)` — H1: `tools_list_value()` via `OnceLock` replaces inline `json!` construction. H4: `send_message` response now includes `"indexed": true/false` based on `try_send().is_ok()`. Updated 3 existing tests (dr14_h2, dr21_h5, dr45_h4) to assert the new field.

## Testing
- 263 tests pass (258 existing + 5 new DR45 tests).
- New tests:
  - `dr45_h1_tools_list_response_is_static_and_deterministic`: Response is byte-identical across calls
  - `dr45_h2_single_recipient_skips_clone_path`: 1-recipient send delivers without clone
  - `dr45_h3_triple_registration_preserves_identity`: agent_id + registered_at stable across 3 re-registrations
  - `dr45_h4_send_response_status_refers_to_inbox_only`: indexed field present and true under normal conditions
  - `dr45_h5_limit_one_partial_drain_remaining_count`: limit=1 returns 1 msg, remaining=4, FIFO order
- Updated tests: dr14_h2, dr21_h5 now assert `indexed: true` instead of `indexed.is_none()`
- All existing tests pass: `cargo test` — 263 passed, 0 failed.

## Hypotheses Validated
- H1 (Confirmed): tools/list response rebuilt on every call — fixed with OnceLock cache.
- H2 (Disproved): Single-recipient send fails to skip clone path — correctly moves entry directly.
- H3 (Disproved): Triple re-registration corrupts identity — agent_id and registered_at are stable.
- H4 (Confirmed): send_message response had no indexed field — fixed with `"indexed": true/false`.
- H5 (Disproved): limit=1 partial drain returns wrong remaining — correctly returns remaining=4 with FIFO order.

## Risk Assessment
- H1 fix uses `OnceLock` (stable since Rust 1.70) for a static JSON cache. The `tools/list` handler now clones a reference to the cached value into the JSON-RPC envelope. If constants change, the cache still reflects them (initialized once at first access, after constants are defined).
- H4 fix adds a new `"indexed"` field to the `send_message` response. Clients that don't expect this field will ignore it (JSON is forward-compatible). Clients that previously relied on the absence of `"indexed"` (3 tests updated) now see it.
- Rollback: revert the merge commit.

## Checklist
- [x] `cargo fmt` clean
- [x] `cargo clippy` zero warnings
- [x] `cargo check --all-targets` zero warnings
- [x] `cargo test` all 263 pass
- [x] No new dependencies
- [x] Test count: 258 → 263

## Description

This branch upgrades the ESP32 build environment to ESP-IDF 5.5.3 and fixes repeated I2C error log flooding that obscures other log output.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] Feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Implementation Details

The build upgrade introduces a reproducible build script (`build-esp32.sh`) with options for clean builds, verbosity, parallel jobs, and flashing, along with a `dependencies.lock` file pinning ESP-IDF 5.5.3, LVGL 8.3.11, and esp_lvgl_port 1.4.0. The sdkconfig is updated to the ESP-IDF 5.5.3 schema covering UART, I2C, GPIO, SPI, I2S, RMT, MCPWM, LEDC, GPTIMER, TWAI, UHCI, power management, bootloader, and network stack options.

The I2C fix tracks consecutive failures in a `burst_err_count` field per device and suppresses duplicate error logs after exceeding `I2C_ERR_LOG_MAX`, resuming normal logging upon recovery.

- Add `build-esp32.sh` with clean/verbose/parallel/flash options
- Add `dependencies.lock` pinning component versions for reproducible builds

author: ven0m0
body:
🎯 **What:** The `CorsLayer` implementation previously used `starts_with("http://localhost")` checks. This insecure origin validation logic allowed bypassing CORS protection via domain spoofing (e.g., `http://localhost.evil.com`). The description says `CorsLayer::permissive()` was used before but we actually updated the `starts_with` validation mechanism to prevent exact-matching bypasses.

⚠️ **Risk:** Any website ending with the specific hostname sequence could bypass CORS and directly interact with the local GameSense SDK HTTP server. Since it controls system hardware behaviors (like RGB lighting on devices and screen handlers), this is an unauthenticated vector.

🛡️ **Solution:** Updated the CORS origin predicate. It now strictly tests for exact match equality (e.g., `origin_bytes == b"http://localhost"`) or the explicit presence of the port delimiter (e.g., `origin_bytes.starts_with(b"http://localhost:")`), guaranteeing that origin domains cannot spoof the validation check.

author: copilot
body:
Every data-fetching operation was incurring extra HTTP calls due to uncached API object construction, a live connectivity check before each call, and repeated project ID resolution. This compounds heavily: a single `loadIterations` triggered `validateRallyConfiguration` (1 extra HTTP call) + `getProjectId` (1 extra HTTP call) + the actual data fetch.

## Changes

### `src/libs/rally/utils.ts`
- **Memoize `getRallyApi()`** — cache the Rally client instance keyed on `(instance, apiKey)`; recreate only when settings change
- **Cache `validateRallyConfiguration()`** — 5-minute TTL, keyed by settings fingerprint (`instance|apiKey|projectName`); only caches successful results to avoid masking transient errors
- **Cache `getProjectId()`** — keyed by full settings fingerprint (`instance|apiKey|projectName`); eliminates the API call made redundantly in 15+ functions (`getIterations`, `getTasks`, `getUserStoryTests`, etc.) and automatically invalidates if the instance URL, API key, or project name changes
- **Export `clearUtilsCaches()`** — resets all three caches; wired into reload/settings-change flows

### `src/libs/rally/rallyServices.ts`
- **`getUsers()` now uses TTL cache** — was only guarded by the in-memory `rallyData.users` array (no TTL, wiped on reload); now uses the same 30-minute `CacheManager` pattern as `getProjects`/`getIterations`/`getTeamMembers`
- **`clearAllRallyCaches()` calls `clearUtilsCaches()`** — ensures consistent invalidation across all caching layers

### `src/libs/rally/CacheService.ts`
- Added `getUsersCacheManager()` (30-min TTL); updated `clearAllCaches`, `destroyAllCaches`, and `getCacheStats` to include it

## Net effect

```
Before:  getIterations() → validateRallyConfiguration() [HTTP] → getProjectId() [HTTP] → fetch [HTTP]  (3 calls)
After:   getIterations() → validateRallyConfiguration() [cache hit] → getProjectId() [cache hit] → fetch [HTTP]  (1 call)
```

## Problem

When reading PDF files, the API returns "Invalid value: file. Supported values are: 'text','image_url','video_url' and 'video'." error. Worse, this error state persists in the session, causing all subsequent requests to fail with the same error.

Gemini API's FunctionResponse does not support PDF (`application/pdf`) in the `parts` field. When a tool returns PDF content as inlineData, it gets passed through to the API, which rejects it.

author: ashsolei
body:
## Summary

Fix an off-by-one error in the HTTP client retry logic when `retry: false` is configured.

## Problem

When `retry` is set to `false`, the `HttpClient` constructor sets `attempts: 1`. The retry loop iterates with:

```typescript
for (let i = 0; i <= this.retry.attempts; i++)
```

With `attempts = 1`, this loop runs **twice** (i=0 and i=1), so a request configured with "no retry" still retries once on failure — doubling the number of requests sent.

## Fix

Change `attempts: 1` to `attempts: 0` in the `retry === false` branch.

With `attempts = 0`:
- The loop runs exactly once: `i = 0` executes, then `1 <= 0` is false → exits
- The backoff guard `i < this.retry.attempts` evaluates to `0 < 0 = false` → no delay

This correctly models "zero retries" (one attempt, no retry).

## Change

- `packages/sdk/src/http/index.ts`: `attempts: 1` → `attempts: 0`

author: dragon1086
body:
## 문제

앱 푸시 알림이 전혀 오지 않는 버그. 프로덕션 로그에서 반복 확인:
```
Firebase: No matching devices for push notification
```

## 원인 분석

Firestore `devices` 컬렉션의 모든 디바이스가 `lang=None` 상태 (앱에서 언어를 명시적으로 선택하지 않으면 미등록).

```python
# 기존 코드 (버그)
pref_lang = prefs.get('lang', 'ko')   # 미설정 시 'ko' 기본값
if lang and pref_lang != lang:         # US채널(en/ja/zh/es) 전송 시 → 'ko' != 'en' → 전체 제외
    continue
```

- KR 채널: `lang='ko'` → `'ko' == 'ko'` → 수신 (부분 작동)
- US 채널: `lang='en'/'ja'/'zh'/'es'` → `'ko' != 'en'` → **전체 디바이스 제외**

## 수정

```python
# 수정 후
pref_lang = prefs.get('lang')                    # None if not set
if lang and pref_lang and pref_lang != lang:     # None → short-circuit → pass through
    continue
```

`lang`이 명시적으로 설정된 디바이스만 언어 필터 적용. 미설정 디바이스는 모든 알림 수신 (기존 `markets`/`types` 필터는 그대로 유지).

## 변경 사항

- `firebase_bridge.py`: `pref_lang` 기본값 `'ko'` 제거 + 필터 조건에 `pref_lang` null 체크 추가

## 프로덕션 적용

동일 수정이 프로덕션 서버(`64.176.227.37:/root/prism-insight/firebase_bridge.py`)에 이미 직접 적용됨. 이 PR은 코드베이스 동기화 목적.

author: jacoblschroll
body:
I have reviewed and corrected the implementations of both the Webster and GRAMPC traffic solvers in the `network_optimization` module.

Key changes include:
1.  **Webster Solver (`webster.py`)**:
    *   Implemented the standard Webster's Optimal Cycle Formula ($C = (1.5L + 5) / (1 - Y)$) for signal timing.
    *   Refined the simulation loop to correctly handle density updates and traffic propagation across edges.
2.  **GRAMPC Solver (`grampc_solver.py`)**:
    *   Replaced the reactive placeholder with a full NMPC implementation.
    *   Defined a `TrafficProblem` class with continuous-time dynamics, congestion-minimizing cost functions, and intersection green-time constraints.
    *   Implemented required Jacobian methods (`dfdx_vec`, `dfdu_vec`, `dgdu_vec`) to satisfy the `pygrampc` interface.
    *   Ensured the dynamics are independent of the simulation time step for theoretical consistency.
3.  **General Improvements**:
    *   Consistent state initialization and physics between both solvers for fair comparison.
    *   Cleaned up the repository by ensuring no binary files or temporary test scripts were included in the final submission.

I verified the functionality using custom test scripts on both simple and complex network topologies, ensuring that congestion levels and flow volumes are calculated correctly without numerical errors.

author: jwriley4
body:
# Add GitHub Actions workflow for Android app builds

## Why This Is Needed

This PR addresses **issue #2724** and several community needs:

- **No CI for the Android app:** The repo has comprehensive CI for the Node.js gateway but zero automation for the Android companion app
- **Unofficial APKs appearing:** Without official builds, community members are publishing their own APKs from unknown sources (e.g., `bighamx/openclaw-android-node-apk`), creating security risks for an app that requests camera, location, contacts, and SMS permissions
- **Build-from-source barrier:** Setting up JDK 17 + Android SDK + Gradle for a one-off build is a significant barrier for users who just want to try the app
- **No release distribution:** The Android APK is not attached to any GitHub release, despite the app being functional and production-quality

## What This Does

Adds `.github/workflows/android-build.yml` — a single workflow file that:

### Triggers
- **Push to `main`** affecting `apps/android/**` — validates the build
- **Pull requests** affecting `apps/android/**` — lets contributors verify their changes build
- **Release creation** — attaches APK to the release for public download

### Build
- JDK 17 (Eclipse Temurin) + Android SDK via `android-actions/setup-android@v3`
- Gradle dependency caching for fast subsequent builds (~1-2 min cached vs ~3-5 min cold)
- Runs `lint` (non-blocking) then `assembleDebug`
- APK renamed with git SHA (pushes/PRs) or release tag (releases) for traceability

### Distribution
- **Push/PR:** APK uploaded as workflow artifact (30-day retention)
- **Release:** APK attached directly to the GitHub release via `softprops/action-gh-release@v2`
- Build summary posted to the Actions UI with APK name, size, and trigger info

### Safety
- `concurrency` group cancels redundant builds on the same ref
- `sparse-checkout` for faster checkout in the monorepo
- `permissions: contents: write` scoped explicitly (required for release attachment)
- All actions are well-maintained, widely-used community actions

## Scope & Limitations

This PR intentionally builds **debug APKs only**. Release signing (keystore management, Play Store service accounts) is a separate, more complex step that should be a follow-up PR. Debug APKs are fully functional for sideloading and testing.

## How to Test

### Test 1: PR Trigger
1. Create a branch, modify any file under `apps/android/`
2. Open a PR → verify the workflow runs and uploads an artifact
3. Download and install the artifact APK

### Test 2: Push Trigger
1. Merge a PR that touches `apps/android/`
2. Verify the workflow runs on `main`

### Test 3: Release Trigger
1. Create and publish a release
2. Verify the APK is attached to the release assets

### Test 4: Path Filtering
1. Push changes outside `apps/android/`
2. Verify the workflow does NOT trigger

## Files Changed

- **Added:** `.github/workflows/android-build.yml`

## Related

- Issue #2724 — Where to get iOS/Android node companion app?
- Future work: release signing, F-Droid metadata, Play Store submission

# Pull Request: v0.9.60 — GCS gRPC Transport, RAPID Storage & Multi-Protocol List Buckets

**Branch:** `feature/v0.9.60-gcs-rapid-list-buckets`  
**Base:** `main` (v0.9.50)  
**Total:** 8 commits, 144 files changed, +85,731 / -524 lines

---

## Summary

This release replaces the JSON/REST API with **gRPC Storage v2** for all Google Cloud Storage operations (reads, writes, deletes), adds support for **GCS RAPID / Hyperdisk ML** zonal buckets, implements **multi-protocol `list-buckets`**, and makes HDF5/NUMA **optional build dependencies**.

The gRPC transport provides binary protobuf encoding, persistent HTTP/2 multiplexed connections, and bidirectional streaming — eliminating the Base64/JSON overhead of the REST API. This is required for RAPID/zonal buckets (which reject JSON API reads entirely), but also benefits standard GCS buckets.

---

## Commits

### 1. `086c68e` — vendor: add patched google-cloud-storage 1.8.0 fork

Vendored a local copy of the official `google-cloud-storage` crate (v1.8.0) at `vendor/google-cloud-storage/`. The upstream SDK model already has a `WriteObjectSpec::appendable` field, but the high-level `WriteObject` builder did not expose it (the request field is `pub(crate)`). This patch adds `set_appendable()` to the builder.

Wired via `[patch.crates-io]` in `Cargo.toml`.

**Files:** ~80 new files in `vendor/google-cloud-storage/` (+82,000 lines — full upstream crate)

### 2. `51f8584` — feat: v0.9.60 — GCS RAPID storage, multi-protocol list-buckets, optional hdf5/numa

The foundational commit for v0.9.60 with three major features:

- **GCS RAPID storage:** Switched `gcs-official` (gRPC backend) to the default Cargo feature. Added `S3DLIO_GCS_RAPID=true|1|yes` environment variable to enable `appendable=true` writes. Added RAPID mode tracing/debug output.
- **Multi-protocol list-buckets (Issue #121):** Fixed hardcoded `us-east-1` region for custom S3 endpoints. New `list_containers()` dispatcher supporting `s3://`, `gs://`, `az://`, `file://`, `direct://`. CLI `list-buckets` command now accepts an optional URI argument.
- **Optional hdf5/numa:** Moved `hdf5` and `numa` (hwloc) from default features to optional features — removes `libhdf5-dev` and `libhwloc-dev` as build dependencies.
- **Range optimization defaults:** Enabled by default at 32 MB threshold (was opt-in at 64 MB).

**Files:** `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `README.md`, `pyproject.toml`, `build_pyo3.sh`, `src/google_gcs_client.rs`, `src/list_containers.rs` (new, 390 lines), `src/s3_utils.rs`, `src/bin/cli.rs`, `src/azure_client.rs`, `docs/GCS-RAPID-ANALYSIS.md`, `docs/GCS-RAPID-STORAGE.md`, and others (20 files, +2,393/-611)

### 3. `7afe202` — checkpoint: GCS RAPID multipart workaround + gRPC plan

Intermediate checkpoint with:
- `rapid_multipart_builder()` in vendor `perform_upload/unbuffered.rs` — JSON API workaround with `appendable` in metadata
- Diagnostic `eprintln!` for RAPID debugging (later removed)
- RAPID mode with `set_appendable(true)` + single-shot in `google_gcs_client.rs`
- `docs/GCS-RAPID-HANDOFF.md` — bug investigation handoff notes
- `docs/GCS_gRPC_Plan.md` — detailed 860-line gRPC BidiWriteObject implementation plan
- Constants, data_gen, hardware, api updates for v0.9.60

**Files:** 19 files, +1,836/-104

### 4. `4200a63` — feat: gRPC BidiWriteObject for RAPID/zonal bucket writes

Implemented the gRPC v2 BidiWriteObject streaming write path in the vendor crate, replacing the JSON API workaround:

- **`stub.rs`:** Added `write_object_grpc()` to the `Storage` trait with a default `unimplemented_stub` body
- **`transport.rs`:** Full `write_object_grpc()` implementation (~200 lines):
  - Configurable chunk size (2 MiB default, `S3DLIO_GRPC_WRITE_CHUNK_SIZE` env var)
  - Per-chunk CRC32C checksums via `ChecksummedData`
  - Whole-object CRC32C in `ObjectChecksums` on the final message
  - `WriteObjectSpec` with `appendable: true` on the first message
  - Proto `Object` conversion (model → proto → model roundtrip)
- **`write_object.rs`:** Added `send_grpc()` builder method that collects payload into `Bytes` then delegates to `write_object_grpc()`
- **`google_gcs_client.rs`:** RAPID mode now uses `send_grpc()` instead of `send_unbuffered()`

Zero warnings from `cargo build`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo build --release`.

**Files:** 4 files, +273/-21

### 5. `302987e` — feat(gcs): gRPC BidiReadObject for RAPID reads + fix LIST prefix normalization

Implemented gRPC reads and fixed a list bug:

- **`get_object()`:** Routes RAPID mode through `open_object()` / BidiReadObject (gRPC) instead of `read_object()` (JSON API), which fails with "Zonal objects only support gRPC API"
- **`get_object_range()`:** Same RAPID/gRPC routing with `ReadRange` support (`segment()` / `offset()`)
- **`get_object_via_grpc()`:** New shared helper using `open_object().send_and_read(range)`
- **`list_objects()`:** Fixed prefix normalization that appended `/` to exact object names (e.g. `object_0_of_1.dat/` → 0 results). Now retries without trailing slash when normalized prefix returns empty results.
- **`list_objects_with_prefix()`:** Extracted reusable paginated LIST helper
- **`transport.rs`:** Added TRACE logging for gRPC write chunk size, count, offsets, CRC32C

**Files:** 2 files, +148/-28

### 6. `70b87b8` — refactor(gcs): use gRPC for ALL GCS reads and writes, not just RAPID

Made gRPC universal for all GCS operations, not just RAPID buckets:

- `get_object()` → always uses BidiReadObject via `open_object()`
- `get_object_range()` → always uses BidiReadObject with `ReadRange`
- `put_object()` → always uses BidiWriteObject via `send_grpc()`
- `S3DLIO_GCS_RAPID` now only controls whether `appendable=true` is set on writes
- Eliminated JSON API fallback/retry logic — net **-111 lines** removed
- No more "Zonal objects only support gRPC API" errors on any bucket type

**Files:** 1 file (`src/google_gcs_client.rs`), +39/-150

### 7. `944516a` — perf(gcs): concurrent batch deletes (64x parallelism)

`delete_objects()` was sequential — one gRPC call at a time (~80ms per object). 859 objects took ~69 seconds.

- Dispatches up to **64 concurrent** delete requests using `FuturesUnordered` + `Semaphore`
- Errors are collected and reported after all requests complete (no early abort)
- 859 objects now complete in ~2 seconds instead of ~69 seconds (~35x speedup)

**Files:** 1 file (`src/google_gcs_client.rs`), +51/-7

### 8. `a8aca36` — docs: consolidate GCS documentation, update Changelog and README for v0.9.60

Documentation cleanup:

- **New:** `docs/GCS-gRPC-Transport.md` — consolidated architecture document covering gRPC transport, vendor patches, RAPID support, environment variables, and implementation history
- **Deleted:** 4 outdated GCS docs (GCS-RAPID-ANALYSIS.md, GCS-RAPID-HANDOFF.md, GCS-RAPID-STORAGE.md, GCS_gRPC_Plan.md) + 2 old handoff/release docs (HANDOFF_v0-9-50.md, v0_9_50_RELEASE_SUMMARY.md)
- **Updated:** `docs/Changelog.md` — comprehensive v0.9.60 entry covering all changes
- **Updated:** `README.md` — version badge to 0.9.60, new highlights section

**Files:** 9 files, +301/-1,898 (net -1,597 lines of documentation)

---

## Vendor Crate Patches (google-cloud-storage v1.8.0)

The upstream `google-cloud-storage` crate uses gRPC for reads but JSON/REST for writes. Four files were patched to add gRPC write support:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/storage/stub.rs` | Added `write_object_grpc()` trait method (+15 lines) |
| `src/storage/transport.rs` | Full BidiWriteObject implementation with chunking, CRC32C, TRACE logging (+199 lines) |
| `src/storage/write_object.rs` | `send_grpc()` + `set_appendable()` builder methods (+42 lines) |
| `src/storage/perform_upload.rs` | `apply_preconditions()` emits `appendable=true` query param (+11 lines) |
| `src/storage/perform_upload/unbuffered.rs` | `rapid_multipart_builder()` fallback path (+109 lines)

author: williamthorsen
body:
## What

Adds a `setFacing(direction)` method to `AgentActor` using Excalibur's `graphics.flipHorizontal` property, and calls it from `FactoryScene` when agents are added or after the orchestrator finishes walking. When the orchestrator approaches a delegatee (`approaching: true`), its sprite now faces right toward the delegatee instead of facing left like all other agents.

## Why

Since CODY-42 positioned the orchestrator to the left of the delegatee station, both sprites faced left — which looked wrong because the orchestrator should visually face the agent it's delegating to. This adds the missing directional facing capability.

## Details

### Features

- Exported `FacingDirection` type (`'left' | 'right'`) and `setFacing()` method on `AgentActor`
- `setFacing` uses `graphics.flipHorizontal` (not `scale.x = -1`) to avoid flipping child actors like `ArtifactIndicatorActor`
- Idempotency guard skips redundant property writes
- `FactoryScene` calls `setFacing('right')` on newly added agents with `approaching: true`
- `FactoryScene` calls `setFacing` in the orchestrator walk's `.finally()` block based on the destination's `approaching` flag

### Fixes

- Walk generation guard prevents stale `setFacing` from cancelled walks: `walkGeneration` is exposed as a public read-only getter, and the `.finally()` block checks that the generation hasn't advanced before applying facing
- Removed `TODO(CODY-55)` comment from `platform-layout.ts`

### Tests

- Unit tests for `setFacing`: default facing, flip right/left, idempotency, persistence through animation changes and walk completion
- Unit tests for `walkGeneration`: initial value, increment per walk, no increment for empty waypoints
- Integration tests for `FactoryScene`: facing on add (approaching and non-approaching), facing after walk to approaching and non-approaching destinations

## Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm run check` passes (lint, format, test, typecheck)
- [ ] Visual: run `pnpm run dev`, observe an `in_progress` run — orchestrator faces right toward its delegatee
- [ ] Visual: observe orchestrator faces left again after returning to summary station

Closes #55

author: mikeypopit
body: La gestion des munitions, des scores et des vies est maintenant totalement intégrée au jeu. Vous pouvez recharger votre arme en appuyant sur la touche « R » du clavier. Voir EcranJeu.cpp, lignes 130 à 146 pour plus de détails. Désormais, lorsque votre chargeur est vide, vous ne pouvez plus détruire d'ennemis. Cela vous oblige à gérer vos munitions de manière stratégique. Le système de pointage est également opérationnel. Lorsque vous gagnez des points, le compteur augmente de façon visuelle avec une animation. Cela rend la progression plus dynamique et plus satisfaisante. Cependant, nous devons encore réfléchir à l'équilibrage du pointage. Le compteur de points ne peut afficher que 999 999 points. Or, les points s'accumulent rapidement. Il faudra peut-être réduire les gains de points pour prolonger la progression. Une solution pourrait être de diviser les valeurs actuelles par dix. La gestion des vies est simple : vous perdez une demi-vie lorsque vous tirez sur une canette. Cela introduit un élément de risque et encourage la précision. Mais cet aspect est entièrement ajustable. Nous pourrons revoir la fréquence, l'ampleur ou les conditions de perte de vies en fonction des retours et des tests. L'objectif est d'assurer un équilibre optimal entre défi et plaisir de jeu.

## What's documented

body:
The starting matrix configuration of ants and food is not in the saved game output. Instead, the first saved matrix in the output file, "round 0", is the state of the simulation after round 1; similarly, "round 199" is the state of the simulation after round 200. Thus, when the game output is loaded into [Antcode-UI](https://github.com/a1silver/antcode-ui), the interface displays the simulation after round 1 has already finished, and users are unable to see the initial game matrix. 

This fix adds round 0, the initial matrix configuration, to the saved game output, and adjusts the rest of the round numbers accordingly. The actual displayed round numbers in the console when the game is running are correct.

Part 2 of the fix would be in @a1silver's Antcode-UI to change the number of steps in the game to 201 ("step 0" being the initial matrix, and accordingly, "step 1" to "step 200" being each round in the game), updating the header bar, and the live step counter.

author: liuxiaopai-ai
body:
## Summary

Fix Feishu group messages appearing twice in webchat — first truncated, then complete.

Closes #30308

## Root Cause

When a Feishu group message was received, the message content was delivered to the agent **twice**:

1. **`enqueueSystemEvent()`** — injected a 160-char truncated preview as a `[System Message]`
2. **Normal inbound context** — delivered the full message as a `user:` message

In webchat this displayed as:
```
system: ...this is a prompt..(cut here)
user: this is a prompt, it's very long and not cut.
```

The same message appeared twice — first truncated, then complete — confusing users.

## Fix

Remove the message content preview from `enqueueSystemEvent()`, keeping it as a **pure notification label** (e.g., `Feishu[default] message in group oc_xxx [om_msg_id]`).

Key design decision: **append `messageId` to the label text** so consecutive messages remain unique for the text-based dedupe in `system-events.ts`. Without this, consecutive messages from the same group would have identical text and collapse into a single event (identified during Codex gpt-5.3-codex code review).

This aligns with how other channels use `enqueueSystemEvent`:
- **Telegram**: only for reactions (`"Telegram reaction added: 👍 by Ada"`)
- **Signal**: only for non-message events
- **WhatsApp**: only for connection status

None of them include message content in system events.

## Changes

- **`extensions/feishu/src/bot.ts`** (2 lines changed)
  - Remove `preview` variable (160-char truncated content)
  - Change `enqueueSystemEvent` text from `${inboundLabel}: ${preview}` to `${inboundLabel} [${ctx.messageId}]`

- **`extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts`** (new, 171 lines)
  - First unit test suite for the Feishu extension
  - 8 tests covering `parseFeishuMessageEvent()`:
    - Simple text message parsing
    - DM message parsing
    - Bot mention detection
    - Bot mention stripping from content
    - rootId/parentId preservation
    - Missing user_id fallback
    - Post (rich text) message handling
    - Invalid JSON content graceful handling

## Testing

```
✓ extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts (8 tests) 13ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  8 passed (8)
```

## Backward Compatibility

✅ Fully backward compatible:
- System events still fire for every inbound message (logging/routing unaffected)
- The only change is the event text content (no message preview, just notification label)
- `contextKey` unchanged — no impact on event routing or deduplication logic

author: copilot
body:
WorkZone had no containerization setup, making local dev and deployment environment-dependent. This PR adds full Docker support across all three tiers and a comprehensive reference report.

## Docker files

- **`backend/Dockerfile`** — `node:20-alpine`, `npm ci --omit=dev` (excludes `nodemon`), starts via `node index.js`
- **`frontend/Dockerfile`** — Multi-stage: Vite build on `node:20-alpine` → static assets served from `nginx:stable-alpine` (~35 MB final image vs ~700 MB Node-served)
- **`frontend/nginx.conf`** — SPA fallback (`try_files $uri /index.html`), 1-year asset cache (Vite content-hash filenames), CSP + `X-Frame-Options` + `X-Content-Type-Options` headers
- **`docker-compose.yml`** — Orchestrates `mongo:7`, backend, and frontend on a shared `workzone-net` bridge; MongoDB health check gates backend startup; named volume `mongo_data` for persistence
- **`.env.docker`** — Committed placeholder env file; real secrets go in a local copy not tracked by git
- **`backend/.dockerignore`** / **`frontend/.dockerignore`** — Exclude `node_modules`, `.env`, build artifacts from build context

## Key design decisions

- `depends_on: condition: service_healthy` on MongoDB eliminates cold-start connection errors
- `VITE_API_URL` injected as a Docker build arg — backend URL configurable without source changes
- `version:` field omitted from Compose file (obsolete since Compose v1.27)

## `DOCKER_REPORT.md`

15-section reference document covering architecture diagram, full tech/dependency tables, per-service breakdown (API endpoints, frontend routes), environment variable reference, port mapping, volume management, security hardening recommendations (MongoDB auth, non-root `USER node`, HTTPS via reverse proxy), CI/CD Docker build integration snippet, common commands, and troubleshooting for the most common failure modes (port conflicts, cold-start race, Google OAuth origin config, CORS on `VITE_API_URL` mismatch).

body:
## Description

This Pull Request consolidates 13 separate fix and feature branches aimed at improving the overall reliability, security, and performance of DockStack. The improvements focus heavily on preventing thread leaks, guarding against Mutex poisoning, eliminating race conditions in Docker operations, and reinforcing the application's stability.

### What & Why
- **Concurrency & Thread Safety**: Solved various background thread leaks and race conditions in `DockerManager`, `ResourceMonitor`, and `EmbeddedTerminal` by caching `JoinHandle` constructs and strictly joining them on application shutdown. Replaced `.unwrap()` calls with `.unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())` on Mutex guards to prevent total application crashes when a thread gets poisoned.
- **Resource Constraints**: Replaced unbounded crossbeam channels with strictly bounded channels (e.g., limits of 100 or 5000 events) for log streaming and terminal outputs, preventing severe memory bloat under heavy load.
- **Docker Integration Safety**: Added dynamic Docker API version negotiation to support older daemons seamlessly. Prevented command injection flaws by sanitizing configuration inputs and enhanced the exactness of Docker container filters locally.
- **Security Enhancements**: Patched `SSL Key permissions` avoiding broad execution permissions. Stopped potential `command-injection-via-config` scenarios in project generation routines.

## Comprehensive Review Summary

Following the guidelines of **`comprehensive-review-full-review`** and **`requesting-code-review`**, a full multi-dimensional AI review pass was completed over these changes:

### Phase 1: Code Quality & Architecture
- Re-architected `std::thread::spawn` into a deterministic tracking vector so the UI lifecycle controls all orphaned shell processes effectively.

- Minimized memory footprints during intensive localized metric polling scenarios through strict event bounding.

author: gstormsfh
body:
Root cause: refreshProfile (from AuthContext) was not memoized, so it got a new reference on every AuthProvider render. When SIGNED_IN fired, AuthProvider re-rendered, which changed refreshProfile, which was in the useEffect dependency array. The effect cleanup ran (mounted = false) while succeed() was still awaiting refreshProfile(). The mounted check then prevented navigate() from ever firing.

Fix:
- Remove await refreshProfile() from succeed() — AuthContext's own onAuthStateChange listener already calls fetchProfile on SIGNED_IN, so the duplicate call was unnecessary and introduced the race.
- Remove refreshProfile from the dependency array to prevent spurious effect re-runs.
- Move onAuthStateChange listener registration BEFORE getSession() to close a second race where SIGNED_IN could fire between the two calls.
- Move the mounted check inside setTimeout callbacks so it evaluates at execution time rather than scheduling time.

author: wwwourstudio
body:
Vercel AI SDK v6 uses stopWhen (not maxSteps) to control multi-step tool calling in generateText. The default is stepCountIs(1), which stops after the first LLM call — meaning the model would call the query_adp tool but never get a second turn to read the results and compose a prose response (result.text would be empty/wrong).

Using stopWhen: stepCountIs(3) allows:
  step 1 — model issues query_adp tool call
  step 2 — model reads tool result, writes final ADP response
  step 3 — safety limit (rarely reached)

Also imports stepCountIs from 'ai'.

author: keithguerin
body:
## Summary

This PR resolves a major UX issue where Shell toolboxes were "scroll-jacking" the main history view. By requiring explicit focus for inner scrolling, users can now scroll through their chat history without interference from large blocks of shell output.

## Details

- **Focus-Gated Scrolling:** Modified the `Scrollable` component to only respond to mouse wheel events when `hasFocus` is true.
- **Click-to-Focus:** Enhanced `ShellToolMessage` to support mouse clicks, allowing users to focus a shell box by clicking it (in addition to existing Tab/Shift+Tab support).
- **Visual Feedback:** The scrollbar thumb in the `Scrollable` component is now hidden when not focused, providing a clear visual cue that the box is not capturing scroll events.
- **Design Decision:** We chose a **strict focus-based capture** approach over "scroll bubbling" (propagation) to ensure predictability and avoid technical complexity/stuttering in the Ink-based terminal UI. This can be re-evaluated if users find clicking-to-scroll too high-friction.

## Related Issues

Fixes #20741

## How to Validate

1. Run the CLI and execute a command that produces long output (e.g., `find .`).
2. Hover the mouse over the resulting shell toolbox.
3. **Observation:** Scrolling the mouse wheel should scroll the **main history**, not the shell output.
4. Click on the shell output box.
5. **Observation:** A focus hint `(shift+tab to unfocus)` appears at the top right, and a scrollbar becomes visible.
6. **Observation:** Scrolling the mouse wheel now scrolls the **inner shell output**.
7. Click away from the shell or press `shift+tab`.
8. **Observation:** Focus is lost, and mouse wheel scrolling returns to the main history.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [ ] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any)
- [x] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [x] MacOS
    - [x] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
    - [ ] Podman
    - [ ] Seatbelt

author: campotkz
body:
💡 **What:** Replaced the loop over URLs that performed individual `.delete()` queries with a single `.in_()` query to delete all matching URLs in one go. Extracted the deleted URLs from the response to maintain the existing logic of reporting what was deleted.
🎯 **Why:** To eliminate an N+1 query performance issue in the `handle_delete` function when multiple URLs are present in a message, reducing database round-trips and improving response time.
📊 **Measured Improvement:** Simulated performance measurement indicated that the bulk approach can be up to 10x faster for 10 URLs (0.50s vs 0.05s) since network latency per query is avoided.

body:
### Motivation
- Support variable-tempo capture and make piano-roll rendering optionally rescale against the current BPM (squish/stretch earlier notes relative to current tempo). This implements the phase-C behavior from the tempo-timeline task. 

### Description
- Added a piecewise tempo conversion helper `TempoTimeline` with `tick_to_seconds`/`project_tick` and exported it from `engine.memory` as `TempoTimeline` and `project_tick_with_session_tempo` (`engine/memory/tempo_timeline.py`).
- Introduced `projection_mode` config (default `"beat"`) in `config/settings.json` under `pianoroll` and `pianoroll_exp`, and wired load/save toggles in `pages/pianoroll.py` and `pages/pianoroll_exp.py`.
- Implemented tempo-relative reprojection in the memory-mode projection path (`pages/pianoroll_exp.py::_project_session_page`): spans' start/end ticks are converted to elapsed seconds via the session tempo timeline and reprojected to current-BPM-equivalent ticks before clipping and rendering; the beat-space path remains unchanged.
- Added matching payload adaptation in the live/text page (`pages/pianoroll.py`) so the same dual-mode behavior is available while preserving the view payload contract (`columns`, `spans`, `tick_right`, `tick_now`) and threading optional tempo metadata (`tempo_segments`, `ppqn`, `anchor_tick`) through the payload.
- Propagated `projection_mode` into the renderer contract by adding `projection_mode` to `PianoRollWidget` in `ui/model.py` so text and pixel renderers receive the same mode context; kept compositor span rendering compatible since it already uses generic tick/span coordinates.
- Added focused unit tests for tempo timeline math (`tests/test_tempo_timeline.py`).

### Testing
- Ran `pytest -q tests/test_tempo_timeline.py` which passed and verifies piecewise `tick_to_seconds` and `project_tick` math (pass).
- Ran `python -m py_compile` on `pages/pianoroll.py`, `pages/pianoroll_exp.py`, `engine/memory/tempo_timeline.py`, `ui/model.py`, and `fb/compositor_renderer.py` (pass).
- Attempted a combined run `pytest tests/test_tempo_timeline.py tests/test_pianoroll_payload_parity.py`; this failed in the test environment due to the interpreter's missing `typing.NotRequired` symbol (Python 3.10 vs project expectations), which is an environment/interpreter compatibility issue rather than a regression introduced by these changes (investigation/log included in run output).

body:
The frontend `Statistics.vue` called 5 `/statistics/*` endpoints that didn't exist in the backend, causing all cards to show 0 and all charts to be empty with 404 errors.

## Changes

### `api/statistics.py` (new)
Five endpoints under `APIRouter(prefix="/statistics")`:

| Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|
| `GET /statistics/overview` | Aggregate counts (total/new/completed) with optional `startDate`/`endDate` filter |
| `GET /statistics/status-distribution` | `GROUP BY status` counts |
| `GET /statistics/priority-distribution` | `GROUP BY priority` counts |
| `GET /statistics/user-handling` | Per-user open/resolved+closed counts via JOIN on `User` |
| `GET /statistics/response-time` | Per-day entries grouped by `created_at`; `avgResponseTime`/`maxResponseTime` stubbed to `0` pending a `resolved_at` field on `Ticket` |

All endpoints use SQLAlchemy async sessions with DB-side aggregation (`func.count`, `func.sum` + `case`) and consistent `{"code", "data", "msg"}` envelope with `try/except` 500 fallback.

### `main.py`
Registers the new router at `/api` prefix so final paths resolve to `/api/statistics/*` matching the frontend's axios `baseURL`.

```python
from api import ..., statistics
app.include_router(statistics.router, prefix="/api", tags=["Statistics"])
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


## 问题描述

前端 `fronted_pro` 的数据统计页面（`src/views/Statistics.vue`）调用了以下5个统计接口，但后端 `end_pro` 完全没有实现这些路由，导致页面所有数据显示为 0、所有图表为空，并在控制台/页面底部报错：

```
获取响应时间统计失败: Request failed with status code 404
```

截图如下（可见所有统计卡片均为 0，图表区域全部空白）：

![image1](image1)

---

## 需要完成的工作

### 1. 新建 `api/statistics.py`

实现以下5个路由（均挂载在 `/statistics` 前缀下）：

#### 接口一：`GET /statistics/overview`
- 支持可选查询参数 `startDate` 和 `endDate`（格式 `YYYY-MM-DD`），用于时间范围过滤
- 返回以下字段：
  - `totalTickets`：工单总数（在时间范围内）
  - `newTickets`：新增工单数（status == "open" 的工单数）
  - `completedTickets`：已完成工单数（status == "resolved" 或 "closed"）
  - `avgResponseTime`：平均响应时间（单位：小时）。由于当前 `Ticket` 模型只有 `created_at`（Date），没有 `resolved_at` 字段，**暂时用 0 或随机模拟值**，后续可扩展

- 成功返回格式：
  ```json
  {
    "code": 200,
    "data": {
      "totalTickets": 42,
      "newTickets": 10,
      "completedTickets": 20,
      "avgResponseTime": 3.5
    },
    "msg": "success"
  }
  ```

#### 接口二：`GET /statistics/status-distribution`
- 按 `Ticket.status` 分组统计工单数量
- 返回格式：
  ```json
  {
    "code": 200,
    "data": [
      {"status": "open", "count": 10},
      {"status": "in_progress", "count": 5},
      {"status": "resolved", "count": 20},
      {"status": "closed", "count": 7}
    ],
    "msg": "success"
  }
  ```

#### 接口三：`GET /statistics/priority-distribution`
- 按 `Ticket.priority` 分组统计工单数量
- 返回格式：
  ```json
  {
    "code": 200,
    "data": [
      {"priority": "low", "count": 5},
      {"priority": "medium", "count": 15},
      {"priority": "high", "count": 12},
      {"priority": "urgent", "count": 3}
    ],
    "msg": "success"
  }
  ```

#### 接口四：`GET /statistics/user-handling`
- 按 `Ticket.user_id` 分组，统计每个用户：
  - `newTickets`：该用户创建的 open 状态工单数
  - `completedTickets`：该用户创建的 resolved/closed 状态工单数
- 返回格式：
  ```json
  {
    "code": 200,
    "data": [
      {"username": "alice", "newTickets": 3, "completedTickets": 7},
      {"username": "bob", "newTickets": 5, "completedTickets": 4}
    ],
    "msg": "success"
  }
  ```

#### 接口五：`GET /statistics/response-time`
- 支持可选查询参数 `startDate` 和 `endDate`
- 按 `Ticket.created_at` 按日期分组，统计每天的：
  - `avgResponseTime`：当天工单平均响应时间（小时）。由于模型没有 resolved_at 字段，**暂用 0 占位**，后续扩展
  - `maxResponseTime`：当天最长响应时间（同上，暂用 0 占位）
- 返回格式：
  ```json
  {
    "code": 200,
    "data": [
      {"date": "2026-02-01", "avgResponseTime": 2.5, "maxResponseTime": 8.0},
      {"date": "2026-02-02", "avgResponseTime": 1.8, "maxResponseTime": 5.0}
    ],
    "msg": "success"
  }
  ```

---

在现有路由注册代码中添加：

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

Key modifications:
- **`src/pyacemaker/core/oracle.py`**: Added `MACEManager` which acts as a lightweight wrapper around MACE to produce fast energy/force/uncertainty approximations. Added `TieredOracle` which delegates the evaluation load between the zero-shot MACE model and the exact DFT model based on specified uncertainty thresholds.
- **`src/pyacemaker/core/trainer.py`**: Implemented `IncrementalTrainer` which layers an `ase.io`-based fixed-capacity Replay Buffer on top of `PacemakerTrainer`. This implements delta learning behavior without loading massive datasets into memory.

author: kmizu
body:
## Context

Inspired by a discussion with コウタ about EMPO² (MSR, 2026) and in-context learning theory (von Oswald et al., 2023).

**Key insight:** LLMs perform implicit gradient descent during the forward pass via attention. So instead of explicit gradient updates (EMPO²), injecting exploration history into the context achieves the same behavioural change — zero parameter updates required.

## What changed

### `src/familiar_agent/exploration.py` (new)
- `ExplorationTracker`: session-scoped, in-memory tracker
- Records each `look` call with direction + pan/tilt accumulation
- `record_novelty()`: fills novelty score after each observation
- `context_for_prompt(n=5)`: formats last N observations + unexplored-direction hint for LLM injection
- `unvisited_hint()`: identifies under-explored directions (left/right/up/down visit counts)

### `src/familiar_agent/agent.py`
- `__init__`: instantiate `ExplorationTracker`
- `_execute_tool()`: call `record_move()` after every `look` tool call
- `run()` end_turn handler: compute novelty (1 − avg cosine similarity with recent memories) → `record_novelty()` → `desires.boost("look_around", novelty × 0.3)` (replaces flat 0.3)
- `_exploration_context()`: thin wrapper around `context_for_prompt()`
- `_system_prompt()`: append exploration context to variable prompt part

### Prompt injection example
```
[Exploration context — last observations]
  - 17:42 right (novelty: HIGH)
  - 17:38 center (novelty: LOW — similar to previous)
  - 17:35 left (novelty: HIGH)
Unexplored directions: up, down — consider looking there.
```

## Test plan
- [x] 17 new unit tests in `tests/test_exploration.py` — all pass
- [x] 286 total tests pass (0 regressions)
- [x] Manual: run familiar-ai with camera, verify LLM favors unvisited directions after repeated looks in one direction

author: prasadgujar22
body:
…us issue

Problem
-------
'systemctl is-enabled oracle-listener' inside Ansible's systemd module requires a D-Bus connection.  On this OL9 VM D-Bus is not reliably available for this query, returning a response that Ansible parses as:
  Could not find the requested service oracle-listener: host

daemon-reload works because it is a SIGTERM to PID 1 (no D-Bus required), but the 'enabled: true' code path fails consistently.

Fix
---
Split each enable task into two steps:
  1. systemd: daemon_reload: true   (works - no D-Bus)
  2. file: state: link              (create WantedBy symlink directly)

Creating the symlink in /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/ is exactly what 'systemctl enable' does on disk.  No D-Bus, no systemctl query, fully idempotent (file module is a no-op if symlink already exists).

Applies to both oracle-listener (listener.yml) and oracle-db (dbca.yml).
