body:
The `updates_weekly` workflow was failing at `actions/checkout@v6` because the pinned submodule commit for `oswm_codebase` (`026295f...`) no longer exists in the remote, causing a fatal `upload-pack: not our ref` error before any workflow steps could run.

## Changes

- **`actions/checkout@v6`**: Added `submodules: false` to prevent the checkout action from attempting to resolve the stale pinned commit SHA.
- **Setup submodules step**: Replaced `git submodule init && git submodule update` (which would still attempt to fetch the stale ref) with a direct shallow clone from `main`:

```yaml
- name: Setup submodules
  run: |
    rm -rf oswm_codebase
    git clone --depth 1 --branch main https://github.com/kauevestena/oswm_codebase.git oswm_codebase
```

This makes the workflow resilient to stale pinned refs and aligns with the original intent (the previous step was already pulling latest `main` via `git pull -r`).

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Problem
> 
> The `updates_weekly` workflow (`.github/workflows/weekly.yml`) is failing at the `actions/checkout@v6` step with:

> Fetching submodule oswm_codebase
> fatal: remote error: upload-pack: not our ref 026295f11b143932d2f4c46339c77f79710e0410
> ```
> 
> The `actions/checkout@v6` action automatically tries to fetch submodules by default. The parent repo has a pinned submodule commit SHA (`026295f...`) for `oswm_codebase` that no longer exists in the remote (likely due to a force-push or history rewrite on `kauevestena/oswm_codebase`). This causes the checkout to fail before any workflow steps run.
> 
> The workflow already has a manual submodule setup step (lines 35-40) that does `git submodule init && git submodule update` followed by `git pull -r`, but this step never gets reached because the checkout action fails first.
> 
> ## Required Fix
> 
> Make the following changes to `.github/workflows/weekly.yml`:
> 
> 1. **Add `submodules: false`** to the `actions/checkout@v6` step (around line 30-32) to prevent it from automatically trying to fetch the submodule with the stale pinned commit. This ensures the checkout step succeeds.
> 
> 2. **Make the manual submodule setup step more resilient** (lines 35-40). Replace the current approach that relies on `git submodule update` (which still tries to fetch the pinned stale commit) with one that:
>    - Removes the existing submodule directory if present
>    - Clones the `oswm_codebase` repo fresh from the `main` branch directly into the `oswm_codebase` directory
>    
>    The replacement step should look something like:
>    ```yaml

>      run: |
>        rm -rf oswm_codebase
>        git clone --depth 1 --branch main https://github.com/kauevestena/oswm_codebase.git oswm_codebase
>    ```
> 
> This approach ensures the workflow always gets the latest `main` branch of the submodule and is not dependent on any specific pinned commit SHA that may become stale over time. This is appropriate since the existing workflow was already pulling the latest from `main` anyway (via `git pull -r`).

## Description
Implemented a comprehensive code coverage reporting system for the Meridian Backend. This PR adds the necessary infrastructure to track testing quality across all services and introduces a custom, premium HTML dashboard for visualizing results. It also resolves a build-breaking interface mismatch within the DeliveryService test project.

## Changes Made
- **Infrastructure**: Integrated `coverlet.collector` into all 6 test projects (`Assignment`, [Delivery](cci:1://file:///c:/Users/athth/OneDrive/Desktop/Sliit/Projects/Meridian/Meridian-Backend/src/DeliveryService/DeliveryService.Tests/DeliveryManagerServiceTests.cs:133:4-152:6), `Driver`, `Route`, `Tracking`, `Vehicle`) to enable automated coverage tracking.

- **Automation**: Verified the full report generation pipeline using `dotnet test` and `ReportGenerator`.

## How to Test
1. **Build Verification**: Run `dotnet build` and ensure the entire solution (including `DeliveryService.Tests`) compiles without errors.

3. **Generate Dashboard**: Run `reportgenerator -reports:"TestResults\*\coverage.cobertura.xml" -targetdir:"TestResults\CoverageReport" -reporttypes:Html`.

author: copilot
body:
Adds list membership and wildcard pattern matching to the Condition/Precondition DSL. Common enterprise JML scenarios (group membership guards, contractor checks, pattern-based exclusions) previously required host-side workarounds.

## Operators

### Contains / NotContains
- List membership evaluation (case-insensitive)
- Path must resolve to array/list (throws on scalar or hashtable)

```powershell
Condition = @{
  NotContains = @{
    Path  = 'Request.Context.Identity.Entitlements.Id'
    Value = 'CN=BreakGlass-Users,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=com'
  }
}
```

### Like / NotLike
- Wildcard pattern matching (case-insensitive)
- Scalar: direct match
- List: true if ANY element matches (Like) or NO element matches (NotLike)
- Throws on hashtable/dictionary

```powershell
# Guard destructive leaver step
Condition = @{
  All = @(
    @{ Equals = @{ Path = 'Plan.LifecycleEvent'; Value = 'Leaver' } }
    @{
      NotLike = @{
        Path    = 'Request.Context.Identity.Entitlements.Id'
        Pattern = 'CN=HR-*'
      }
    }
  )
}
```

## Implementation

- **Schema validation**: `Test-IdleConditionSchema.ps1` - Added operator shape validation (Path+Value / Path+Pattern)
- **Evaluation logic**: `Test-IdleCondition.ps1` - Implements case-insensitive list/scalar semantics with explicit hashtable rejection
- **Member-access enumeration**: `Get-IdlePropertyValue.ps1` - Enhanced to support property extraction from array items (e.g., `Entitlements.Id` returns array of all Id values)
- **Tests**: 58 new tests covering schema validation, evaluation, edge cases, member-access enumeration, and hashtable rejection
- **Documentation**: `conditions.md`, `context-resolver.md`, and `capabilities.md` updated with operator reference, member-access enumeration explanation, semantics table, corrected path syntax, and troubleshooting guidance for inspecting resolved context data

## Member-Access Enumeration

A critical enhancement to support real-world provider data: entitlements are objects with `Kind`, `Id`, and `DisplayName` properties, not simple strings.

The path resolver now supports PowerShell-style member-access enumeration:
- `Request.Context.Identity.Entitlements` → array of entitlement objects
- `Request.Context.Identity.Entitlements.Id` → array of all Id values
- `Request.Context.Identity.Entitlements.DisplayName` → array of all DisplayName values

This enables the documented use cases to work with realistic provider output.

## Discoverability and Troubleshooting

Added comprehensive guidance for workflow authors to inspect resolved context data:

- **New troubleshooting section** in `context-resolver.md` showing three methods to inspect context structure:
  - `ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5` for full structure inspection
  - `Format-Table -AutoSize` for quick tabular view
  - `Get-Member` for property discovery
- **Enhanced capabilities reference** documenting entitlement object structure with examples
- **Cross-references** between documentation for complete workflow authoring guidance

This addresses the challenge of discovering what data structure is written by context resolvers, enabling admins to determine the correct path syntax for Conditions.

## Additional Changes

Fixed PSSA warnings per CI mode requirements:
- PSUseApprovedVerbs: `Ensure-IdleBlankLineBeforeMarkdownLists` → `Add-IdleBlankLineBeforeMarkdownLists`
- PSUseConsistentIndentation: `Generate-IdleStepReference.ps1`, `New-IdleEntraIDAdapter.ps1`

## Backward Compatibility

Pure additive extension. Existing workflows unchanged. Member-access enumeration is transparent for paths that don't use it.

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>Extend Condition DSL with Contains and Like operators (list-aware evaluation)</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Problem Statement
> 
> The current Condition / Precondition DSL does not provide native support
> for evaluating list membership or wildcard matching on resolved context data.
> 
> Typical real-world use cases include:
> 
> - Execute a step only if the identity is **not member of a specific group**
> - Execute a step only if the identity is **not member of any group matching a pattern**
> - Execute a step only if a string attribute matches a wildcard pattern
> 
> Today, these scenarios require host-side boolean flags or workaround logic,
> which reduces expressiveness and breaks provider-agnostic design principles.
> 
> ## Proposed Solution
> 
> Extend the Condition / Precondition DSL with the following operators:
> 
> - `Contains`
> - `NotContains`
> - `Like`
> - `NotLike`
> 
> ### Semantics
> 
> **Case-insensitive by default.**
> 
> #### Contains / NotContains
> 
> - Intended for **list membership evaluation**
> - Path must resolve to a list
> - `Contains` returns true if the list contains the specified value
> - `NotContains` returns true if the list does not contain the specified value
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```powershell
> Condition = @{
>   NotContains = @{
>     Path  = 'Request.Context.Identity.Entitlements'
>     Value = 'CN=BreakGlass-Users,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=com'
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> #### Like / NotLike
> 
> - Intended for wildcard pattern matching
> - If Path resolves to:
>   - Scalar → evaluate normally
>   - List → evaluate true if **any element** matches the pattern
> 
> Example (list evaluation):
> 
> ```powershell
> Condition = @{
>   NotLike = @{
>     Path    = 'Request.Context.Identity.Entitlements'
>     Pattern = 'CN=HR-*'
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> Example (scalar evaluation):
> 
> ```powershell
> Condition = @{
>   Like = @{
>     Path    = 'Request.Context.Identity.Profile.DisplayName'
>     Pattern = '* (Contractor)'
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> ### Design Principles
> 
> - `All`, `Any`, and `None` remain logical combinators (AND / OR / NOT)
> - No new logical operators introduced
> - No provider changes required
> - Fail-fast if:
>   - `Contains` used on scalar
>   - Invalid Path
>   - Missing Value/Pattern
> 
> ### Applies to
> 
> - `Condition`
> - `Preconditions`
> 
> ## Alternatives Considered
> 
> ### Introduce dedicated operators such as `AnyLike`
> 
> Rejected because:
> 
> - `Any` is a logical combinator (OR), not a comparison operator
> - Overloading it would break DSL consistency
> - Adds unnecessary surface area
> 
> ### Host-side boolean flags
> 
> Rejected because:
> 
> - Breaks provider-agnostic workflow design
> - Pushes logic outside DSL
> - Reduces readability and maintainability
> 
> ## Impact
> 
> - Does not affect existing workflows
> - No breaking changes
> - Pure additive DSL extension
> 
> Backward compatibility: fully preserved.
> 
> ## Additional Context
> 
> This enhancement improves common enterprise scenarios:
> 
> - Joiner / Mover / Leaver group-guard logic
> - Conditional entitlement pruning
> - Pattern-based exclusion rules
> - Safer destructive step gating
> 
> Documentation updates required:
> 
> - Conditions page (new operators section)
> - Preconditions page (reference section)
> - Common Patterns examples
> - Explicit note: `Contains` only valid for lists, `Like` supports scalar and list paths

author: copilot
body:
Adds a Python module for dynamically scheduling requests across Prefill and Decode workers in a vLLM PD-disaggregated inference setup.

### Components (`workspace/tools/vllm_pd_scheduler/`)

- **`models.py`** — `PDInstance`, `InstanceRole`, `SchedulerConfig`, `ScheduleRequest/Result` dataclasses
- **`health.py`** — `HealthChecker` polling vLLM `/health` endpoints, tracking pending requests + KV cache usage, firing status-change callbacks
- **`scheduler.py`** — `PDScheduler` with three strategies: `round_robin`, `least_load` (default), `weighted` (composite score over load, KV cache pressure, heartbeat staleness)
- **`router.py`** — `PDRouter` orchestrating the full P→D pipeline: schedule prefill → forward → extract KV cache token → schedule decode → forward
- **`config.py`** / **`__main__.py`** — JSON config loader and CLI entry point with health-check loop + graceful shutdown

### Usage

```python
from vllm_pd_scheduler.models import InstanceRole, PDInstance
from vllm_pd_scheduler.router import PDRouter
from vllm_pd_scheduler.config import load_config

router = PDRouter(load_config("scheduler_config.json"))
router.register_instance(PDInstance("p0", InstanceRole.PREFILL, "10.0.0.1", 8000))
router.register_instance(PDInstance("d0", InstanceRole.DECODE, "10.0.0.2", 8000))
router.run_health_checks()

result = router.route_request({"prompt": "hello", "max_tokens": 128})
```

Or standalone: `python -m vllm_pd_scheduler --config scheduler_config.json`

### Tests

24 unit tests covering models, all three scheduling strategies, health checker (healthy/unhealthy/draining/callbacks), router (success/prefill-fail/decode-fail/drain), and config loading. Pure stdlib, no external deps.

author: sparktron
body:
### Motivation
- The app was mixing surface and nest visuals in the same render pass causing UI confusion; the goal is to have two distinct 2D views (top-down surface and side-view nest) and ensure only one is active/visible at a time while keeping a shared persistent simulation.
- Toggling must be instant and preserve simulation/cameras/state; input must target only the active view and not leak into the other.

### Description
- Introduced a finite-state `ViewManager` with exactly two states `SURFACE` and `NEST` and an in-code comment block describing what data is shared vs view-specific and coordinate mapping (`src/ui/ViewManager.js`).
- Split rendering into two dedicated renderers: `SurfaceRenderer` and `NestRenderer`, each with its own camera/zoom, `screenToWorld` and draw logic so the app only draws the active view per frame (`src/render/SurfaceRenderer.js`, `src/render/NestRenderer.js`).
- Added a shared simulation abstraction `SimulationCore` that owns the `World`, `Colony`, RNG and tick logic so simulation updates are independent of view toggles (`src/sim/SimulationCore.js`).
- Added `InputRouter` to route pointer/wheel events to the active view handlers only (paint/pan/zoom), preventing input leakage across views (`src/input/InputRouter.js`).
- Refactored `src/main.js` to wire `ViewManager`, the two renderers, `SimulationCore`, and `InputRouter`; the render loop draws only the active renderer, per-view cameras are saved/restored on load, and toggling is exposed via UI and hotkey.
- Updated UI and layout to match the SimAnt feel: left vertical palette (map/tool buttons + health bars), center playfield with a mode banner, right stats/minimap, bottom caste sliders, and a clear `VIEW` toggle button; `TAB` toggles views (`index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/ui/controls.js`, `src/ui/hud.js`).
- Save/load now persists current view and per-view camera transforms so toggles restore exact camera positions (`main.js` save/load changes).

### Testing
- Ran the unit/dev checks: `node --test --experimental-default-type=module test/view-manager.test.mjs` which passed (tests verify view toggling and simulation persistence across toggles).
- Served the app locally with `python3 -m http.server 4173` and validated in a headless browser (Playwright script) that the app initially shows `SURFACE` and pressing `TAB` changes the `#modeIndicator` to `NEST`; this check succeeded and a screenshot was captured.
- Manual runtime smoke: started the app in a browser, exercised `TAB` and the `VIEW` button, confirmed only one renderer draws each frame, per-view camera pans/zoom independently, and simulation state persists across toggles (no resets).

author: ekremney
body:
## Summary

- PostgREST `batchGetByKeys` uses `.in(field, values)` which generates GET URLs like `?id=in.(uuid1,uuid2,...)`. With hundreds of keys, this exceeds HTTP URL length limits causing **414 Request-URI Too Large**.
- Splits the `.in()` call into chunks of 50 keys (~1,800 chars per chunk, well under the 8KB URL limit) and merges results.
- This is a defense-in-depth fix at the data-access layer. All callers of `batchGetByKeys` are now automatically protected. See also #1390 for the TierClient-specific fix.

- [x] New test verifies 120 keys are split into 3 chunks (50 + 50 + 20)

author: kossoy
body:
Implements #103 ## Changes After downloading the tarball, `install.sh` now also downloads `checksums.txt` from the release and verifies the SHA256 hash before extracting. This ensures binary integrity and catches corrupted or tampered downloads. - Downloads `checksums.txt` from the same release tag - Verifies using `sha256sum` (Linux) or `shasum -a 256` (macOS) - Fails the install if the checksum file cannot be downloaded - Prints a warning if neither tool is available (unlikely on supported platforms) ## Testing - Reviewed against the release workflow to confirm `checksums.txt` format matches (`sha256sum *.tar.gz > checksums.txt`) - Verified `--ignore-missing` flag works correctly with multi-binary checksum files - All existing Go tests pass (`go test ./...`) - Binary builds successfully (`go build ./cmd/maestro/`)

Greptile Summary

Added checksum verification to the install script by downloading `checksums.txt` from the GitHub release and verifying the binary's SHA256 hash before extraction. The implementation correctly integrates with the release workflow (which generates checksums using `sha256sum *.tar.gz > checksums.txt`) and handles platform differences between Linux (`sha256sum`) and macOS (`shasum -a 256`). **Key changes:** - Downloads `checksums.txt` from the same release tag as the binary - Verifies checksum using `--ignore-missing` flag to handle multi-platform checksum files - Fails installation if checksums file cannot be downloaded **Issues already raised in previous threads:** - Checksum verification lacks explicit error messaging when verification fails (relies on `set -e` behavior) - Script proceeds with installation if neither `sha256sum` nor `shasum` is available, which bypasses the security feature this PR introduces

Confidence Score: 3/5

- This PR adds important security verification but has error handling concerns that have been previously identified - The implementation correctly adds checksum verification and integrates well with the release workflow. However, the score reflects two significant concerns already raised in previous review threads: (1) implicit error handling that may not provide clear feedback to users when verification fails, and (2) the fallback behavior that continues installation without verification when checksum tools are unavailable, which undermines the security purpose of this change - The `install.sh` file needs attention to address the error handling concerns on lines 57-60 and the security fallback on lines 61-62

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | install.sh | Added SHA256 checksum verification after download, correctly integrates with release workflow format and uses platform-appropriate tools (`sha256sum` or `shasum`) | Last reviewed commit: 3981eba

Every single reference to the original project/author must be replaced. The app must remain fully functional, and a GitHub Pages static landing/demo page must be added. --- ## 🔤 Branding - **New name:** `NoteSync` - **Tagline:** `Real-time collaborative code editor — no database, no setup, just share and code.` - **Author:** `Aviral Bhardwaj` - **GitHub repo URL:** `https://github.com/aviral-bhardwaj/notepad` - **GitHub Pages URL (for static demo):** `https://aviral-bhardwaj.github.io/notepad` - The internal Rust crate/package names (`rustpad-server`, `rustpad-wasm`) can remain the same for technical reasons, but all user-facing strings, comments, and docs must say "NoteSync". --- ## 📝 Files to Change ### 1. `README.md` — Full rewrite Replace the entire README. Remove all references to `ekzhang`, `rustpad.io`, Docker Hub badges pointing to `ekzhang/rustpad`, and the "In the media" section. Write a fresh README as if Aviral built this: ```markdown # NoteSync [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/aviral-bhardwaj/notepad/ci.yml?label=CI)](https://github.com/aviral-bhardwaj/notepad/actions/workflows/ci.yml) **NoteSync** is an _efficient_ and _minimal_ self-hosted collaborative code editor. Share a link, invite collaborators, and edit code together in real time — directly in your browser. No database required. 🌐 **Live Demo:** [aviral-bhardwaj.github.io/notepad](https://aviral-bhardwaj.github.io/notepad) ## How It Works NoteSync uses the **Operational Transformation** algorithm to merge concurrent edits without conflicts. The backend is written in **Rust** using the [warp](https://github.com/seanmonstar/warp) web framework. Text operation logic is compiled to **WebAssembly** via [wasm-bindgen](https://github.com/rustwasm/wasm-bindgen) and runs in the browser. The frontend is built with **React + TypeScript** and powered by the [Monaco Editor](https://github.com/microsoft/monaco-editor) (the same editor that runs VS Code). Documents are stored in-memory and expire after 24 hours of inactivity — no database provisioning needed. ## Tech Stack - **Backend:** Rust, Warp, Tokio, SQLite (optional persistence) - **Frontend:** React 18, TypeScript, Monaco Editor, Chakra UI, Vite - **Real-time:** WebSockets + Operational Transformation - **WASM:** Rust → WebAssembly via wasm-bindgen ## Development Setup You need: Rust, `wasm-pack`, and Node.js (v18+). ```bash # 1. Build the WebAssembly module wasm-pack build rustpad-wasm # 2. Install frontend dependencies npm install # 3. Start the backend server cargo run # 4. In another terminal, start the frontend dev server npm run dev ``` Open [http://localhost:5173](http://localhost:5173) — it hot-reloads on changes. ## Testing ```bash # Backend integration tests cargo test # WebAssembly tests (headless Chrome) wasm-pack test --chrome --headless rustpad-wasm ``` ## Configuration | Variable | Default | Description | |---|---|---| | `PORT` | `3030` | HTTP port to listen on | | `EXPIRY_DAYS` | `1` | Days before inactive documents are garbage collected | | `SQLITE_URI` | _(none)_ | SQLite path for optional persistence across restarts | | `RUST_LOG` | _(none)_ | Logging directives (see [env_logger](https://docs.rs/env_logger/)) | ## Docker Deployment ```bash # Build the image docker build -t notesync . # Run it docker run --rm -dp 3030:3030 notesync ``` Then open [http://localhost:3030](http://localhost:3030). --- <sup>Built by <a href="https://github.com/aviral-bhardwaj">Aviral Bhardwaj</a>. author: aya-kurabuchi115
body:
## Summary

closes #175

セッション切れ時のユーザー体験を大幅に改善するための変更です。

- **middleware**: セッション切れ検出時に `/login?expired=true&redirect={元のパス}` にリダイレクトするように変更
- **ログインページ**: `expired=true` パラメータ検出時に info スタイル（青系）のセッション切れバナーを表示。ログイン成功後に `redirect` パラメータの URL に遷移
- **SSR ページ**: 全ての `redirect("/login")` を `redirectToLogin()` ヘルパーに統一（`src/lib/auth/redirect.ts`）
- **CSR ページ**: `router.push("/login")` に `expired=true&redirect=` パラメータを付与
- **fetchWithAuth()**: API 呼び出しの 401 レスポンスを統一的に検知しセッション切れリダイレクトする共通ラッパー（`src/lib/api-client.ts`）
- **SessionMonitor**: Supabase `onAuthStateChange` の `SIGNED_OUT` イベントをグローバルに監視し、複数タブ間のログアウト同期にも対応（`src/components/session-monitor.tsx`）

### セキュリティ対策
- `redirect` パラメータは相対パス（`/` 開始）のみ許可
- プロトコル相対URL（`//example.com`）やバックスラッシュを拒否
- 許可されたプレフィックス（`/dashboard`, `/interview`, `/profile` 等）のみ遷移可能
- 連続リダイレクト防止（1回のみ実行）

## Test plan
- [ ] セッション切れ後にダッシュボード等にアクセスすると、ログインページに青色のバナー「セッションの有効期限が切れました。再度ログインしてください。」が表示されること

- [ ] 複数タブでログアウトすると他のタブもログインページにリダイレクトされること

author: doruche
body:
This PR introduces the core infrastructure for device management and system initialization, including:

- **Device Driver Model:** Implemented a Linux-like `kobject` base with `bus`, `device`, and `driver` abstractions. Included procedural macros to better simulate OOP patterns and established the initial `platform_bus` architecture.
- **Device Tree Support:** Introduced a new `device-tree` crate capable of parsing FDT data. It performs unflattening into a continuous physical memory arena for efficient access.
- **Hardware Discovery:** Implemented logic to extract devices from the Device Tree and build a hierarchical platform bus structure (treating `simple-bus` compatible nodes as platform buses).
- **Initcall Mechanism:** Added an `initcall` system that allows sub-modules to declare initialization functions with defined priorities, which are automatically invoked during the kernel boot sequence.
- **Drivers & Utils:** Added a skeleton driver for `ns16550a` to validate the probe process and DTB parsing. Introduced `identity` and `as_container` utilities.

author: erinlkolp
body:
## Summary
Enhanced the `require_allowed_user` decorator to properly support modal view handlers by adding an `is_view` parameter that controls pre-acknowledgment behavior and error handling.

## Key Changes
- Added `is_view` parameter to `require_allowed_user()` decorator to distinguish between slash-command/action handlers and modal view handlers
- Modified decorator logic to skip pre-acking when `is_view=True`, allowing view handlers to control their own response (e.g., returning validation errors)
- For unauthorized view submissions, the decorator now calls `ack()` to silently dismiss the modal instead of sending an error message via `respond()`
- Applied the decorator to `handle_edit_note_modal()` and removed the inline authorization check that was previously duplicating this logic
- Added comprehensive test coverage for both authorized and unauthorized view handler scenarios

## Implementation Details
- When `is_view=False` (default): Maintains existing behavior - pre-acks authorized requests and uses `respond()` for unauthorized ones
- When `is_view=True`: Skips pre-ack for authorized requests (handler controls ack/response), and calls `ack()` for unauthorized requests to dismiss the modal silently
- This allows view handlers to return custom `response_action` objects (e.g., validation errors) without interference from the decorator

Automated PR by agent `agent-1`.

**Task:** claim-process-1
**Description:** Business Requirements Document (BRD)
Integrated Policy, Claims, and Payments Platform

Objective
*********
Develop a unified platform for managing insurance policies, claims, and payments. The system must support comprehensive policy lifecycle management, claims processing, and secure payment/disbursement workflows, with robust integration between all modules. The platform must be secure, auditable, responsive, and compliant with regulatory standards.

Functional Requirements
***********************

Access & Authentication
***********************
* Only authorized users with appropriate roles can access policy, claims, and payment modules.
* All actions (search, create, edit, payment, claim) must be logged with user ID and timestamp for audit purposes.

Policy Management
*****************

1. Support creation, retrieval, update, and search of policies.
2. Policy search must allow searching by Policy Number, Insured First Name, Insured Last Name, Policy Type, Loss Date, Policy City, Policy State, Policy Zip, SSN/TIN, and Organizational Name.
3. Support both exact and partial matches for name, policy number, and address.
4. Display policy details including: Insured Name, Policy Number, Policy Type, Effective Date, Expiration Date, Policy Status, Vehicle Details (Year, Make, Model, VIN), Location Details (Address, City, State, Zip), Coverage Details (Types, Limits, Deductibles).
5. SSN/TIN must be masked according to security policies.
6. Allow users to reset all defined search criteria to default/empty values.
7. Policy details must be accessible and compliant with WCAG guidelines.
8. All policy actions must be auditable.

Claims Management
*****************

1. Claims must be linked to policies and support creation, retrieval, update, and search.
2. Claim History must display a list of past claims associated with the policy, showing: Claim Number, Date of Loss, Claim Status.
3. Claims must be sorted by Date of Loss (most recent first) and filterable by Claim Status (Open, Closed, Paid, Denied).
4. Add/Edit policy information at claim level when policy is unverified; changes must be tracked separately and not overwrite original policy data.
5. Visual indicator must show when claim-level policy information is being used.
6. Audit log must track all changes to claim-level policy data, including user and timestamp.
7. Claims must support referral to subrogation and management of scheduled payments (applicability, type, total amount, balance, current due, recipient identification).
8. Claims must support injury incident details, coding information, and carrier involvement.

Payments & Disbursements
************************
1. Payments must be linked to claims and policies, supporting multiple payment methods: ACH, wire, credit/debit card, Stripe Connect, global payouts.
2. Support onboarding of vendors and claimants with secure payment method verification (including KYC/Identity).
3. Enable automated creation of payable line items from external estimates (e.g., Xactimate/XactAnalysis).
4. Allow configuration of payment routing rules based on payee, payment type, and business rules.
5. Provide full payment lifecycle management: creation, voids, reversals, reissues, reserve handling.
6. Enable allocation of payments across multiple reserve lines and management of joint payees.
7. Support creation of Electronic Funds Transfers (EFT) and wire transfers with required banking details.
8. Allow creation of payments with positive, negative, or zero dollar amounts.
9. Support designation of payments as eroding or non-eroding against reserve lines.
10. Enable management of multiple payment details per transaction (add/remove payees, payment portions, deductions).
11. Allow withholding of income tax and designation of payments as tax reportable; capture tax ID numbers for payees.
12. Support document attachment to payment transactions.
13. Remittance & Medical Payments: Support EDI/EOB-style remittances to medical providers, including CPT/ICD mappings and adjustments; integrate with bill review vendors and support EDI 835/837 formats.
14. Negotiation & Settlement Management: Provide negotiation management, coverage opinion requests, and settlement plan tracking.
15. Compliance: Ensure PCI-DSS compliance, mask sensitive payment information, encrypt all payment data in transit and at rest, maintain audit trail for all payment actions and changes.

Integration Requirements
************************

1. Integrate policy, claims, and payment modules for seamless workflow.
2. Integrate with external systems: Stripe Connect, Global Payouts, Bank ACH/Wire, Xactimate/XactAnalysis, Accounting, Bill Review, EDI 835/837, Litigation Data, Tax ID, General Ledger, Agency Markets Payment Service, Document Management.
3. Capture and reuse Other Carrier Information across claim functions, including parties and payments.

Non-Functional Requirements
***************************

1. All interfaces must be responsive and optimized for workflow efficiency.
2. Policy search results must be returned within 3 seconds; policy details and claim history within 5 seconds; payment processing within 5 seconds.
3. System must support concurrent user sessions without performance degradation.
4. All integrations must be robust and support error handling and retry logic.
5. Display must be accessible and compliant with WCAG guidelines.

Error Handling & Messaging
**************************

1. If no matching policies or claims are found, display: "No matching policies/claims found."
2. If the system is unavailable, display: "System is currently unavailable."
3. If policy/claim/payment details cannot be retrieved, display: "Unable to retrieve details. Please try again later."
4. If claim-level policy data cannot be saved, display: "Unable to save claim-level policy data. Please try again later."
5. If no prior claims exist, display: "No prior claims exist for this policy."

Security
********

1. Mask and encrypt sensitive data (SSN/TIN, payment info).
2. Enforce role-based access control.
3. Maintain comprehensive audit logs for all actions.

Audit & Compliance
******************
1. All changes to policy, claim, and payment data must be tracked with user and timestamp.
2. System must comply with PCI-DSS and other relevant standards.

## Fix `end_line` incorrectly assigned from `start_line` in CSV output

In `flatten_scan()` in `src/formattedcode/output_csv.py`, the `end_line` field for copyrights, holders, and authors was assigned `copyr['start_line']` instead of `copyr['end_line']`. This caused the `end_line` column in CSV output to always equal `start_line`, losing the actual end line information for multi-line copyright notices.

The underlying data model (`CopyrightDetection`, `HolderDetection`, `AuthorDetection` in `src/cluecode/copyrights.py`) all define both `start_line` and `end_line` fields, and the JSON output correctly includes both values. Git blame traces this to a copy-paste error in commit `ef8086d` ("Update CSV output to latest copyright data format", ~2018).

Fixes #4785

body:
The repo was nearly empty. This PR builds the complete application from scratch: a dark-themed DeFi SaaS platform with role-based access control, 40+ DEX swap routing UI, flash loans, AI contract builder, template marketplace, and developer tooling.

## Structure
- `package.json` / `vite.config.ts` / `tailwind.config.ts` / `tsconfig.json` — Vite + React 18 + TypeScript + TailwindCSS (dark theme, custom surface/brand palette), path alias `@/ → src/`
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `.env.example`, `.gitignore`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (least-privilege `contents: read` permissions)

## RBAC
Three permission tiers defined in `src/types/roles.ts` and enforced via `ProtectedRoute` + `useRole` hook:

| Tier | Additional access |
|------|------------------|
| `user` | swap, flash loans, contracts, templates |
| `dev` | + API explorer, webhooks, deployments, logs |
| `admin` | + user management, roles, settings, audit log |

Mock auth in `AuthContext` derives role from email prefix (`admin@`, `dev@`, `user@`) — no real Supabase credentials required to run locally.

## Pages (20 total)
- **Public**: Landing (hero + feature grid + stats), Login (email + wallet connect), 404
- **User**: Dashboard (portfolio chart, recent txs, quick actions), Swap (route comparison across providers), Flash Loans (strategy builder + preview), Contract Builder (AI prompt + Solidity editor), Templates (marketplace with category filter)
- **Dev**: Dashboard (API call chart, deployment list), API Explorer (collapsible endpoint browser + live try-it), Webhook Manager (CRUD + toggle), Deployment Status, Logs (level filter)
- **Admin**: Dashboard (stats + user growth chart), User Management (search + delete), Role Permissions (per-resource action grid), System Settings (feature flags), Audit Log

## Components
Reusable primitives in `src/components/ui/`: `Button` (5 variants), `Card`, `Badge`, `Input`, `Modal`, `Sidebar` (collapsible, role-filtered nav), `Header`, `StatsCard`, `Table` (generic typed). `ActivityChart` is a dependency-free inline SVG chart.

## Docs
`README.md` with Mermaid architecture diagram, RBAC table, setup guide, deployment examples (Vercel/Netlify/Docker), and `docs/screenshots/` with 5 SVG dashboard mockups embedded in the README.

author: kitcommerce
body:
## Summary

Removes the hard runtime dependency on  and  so Workarea can run on Rails 7.1+. On Rails < 7.1, behavior is entirely unchanged — rack-cache is still loaded and used exactly as before. On Rails 7.1+, rack-cache is skipped and ActionDispatch's built-in HTTP caching (`stale?`, `fresh_when`, `expires_in`) handles cache semantics.

Closes #688.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `core/lib/workarea/core.rb` | Conditionally `require 'rack/cache'` only on Rails < 7.1 |
| `core/lib/workarea/cache.rb` | Guard `RackCacheKey` class behind `defined?(Rack::Cache::Key)` |
| `core/lib/workarea/configuration/cache_store.rb` | Skip `redis-rack-cache` setup on Rails >= 7.1 |
| `core/config/initializers/10_rack_middleware.rb` | Version-aware Dragonfly middleware placement |
| `core/app/middleware/workarea/application_middleware.rb` | Skip `rack-cache.*` env vars on Rails >= 7.1 |
| `core/workarea-core.gemspec` | Add comment noting conditional load (gem still declared for backward compat) |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] No rack-cache references remain as hard requirements
- [x] `redis-rack-cache` is loaded only when Rails < 7.1
- [x] Rails < 7.1 behavior preserved (zero changes to execution path)
- [ ] Tests pass (run storefront suite to verify)

## Client impact

**High impact — migration required for Rails 7.1+ upgrades.**

For apps upgrading to Rails 7.1+:
1. rack-cache will no longer be active. HTTP caching must be implemented via Rails controller helpers (`stale?`, `fresh_when`, `expires_in`).
2. `Workarea::Cache::RackCacheKey` will not be defined — any app code or plugins extending this class must be updated.
3. `redis-rack-cache` can be removed from application Gemfiles after upgrading.
4. `Workarea::Cache::Varies` continues to work — cache vary logic is still computed, but applications on Rails 7.1+ must propagate it via `Vary` headers or custom logic in controllers.

Apps remaining on Rails 6.1 are unaffected; all behavior is identical to previous releases.

author: copilot
body:
Converts a Google Sheets lunch menu (merged cells, alternating EN/TH rows) into a cached JSON API, consumed by a Chrome extension showing today's or the week's menu.

## Backend (`backend/`)

- **`parser.py`** — Core logic: locates category blocks via column-A merges (dynamic, no hardcoded rows), pairs alternating English/Thai rows into `{en, th}` items, auto-detects Mon–Fri columns from header row
- **`sheets.py`** — Fetches spreadsheet metadata + values via Google Sheets API; selects the correct "ala carte" / "program" tab by title match, preferring the current week's tab
- **`auth.py`** — OAuth token file for local dev; falls back to ADC (service account) when token/credentials files are absent
- **`main.py`** — FastAPI: `GET /health`, `GET /menu` (TTL-cached), `POST /refresh` (protected by `X-Refresh-Token` header)
- **`cache.py`** — Simple in-memory TTL cache (default 6 h, configurable via `CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`)

Example normalised response shape:
```json
{
  "week": { "start": "2026-03-02", "end": "2026-03-06", "label": "2-6 March, 2026" },
  "lastFetched": "2026-03-02T08:00:00+00:00",
  "menus": {
    "alacarte": {
      "days": {
        "monday": [
          { "category": "Thai food", "items": [{ "en": "Pad Thai", "th": "ผัดไทย" }] }
        ]
      }
    }
  },
  "source": { "spreadsheetId": "...", "selectedSheets": [{ "title": "Lunch Ala Carte (Mar 2-6)", "sheetId": 0 }] }
}
```

- **`tests/test_parser.py`** — 16 unit tests covering merge detection, week label parsing (same-month and cross-month), EN/TH pairing, blank-skipping, and odd-row tolerance — no real API calls

## Chrome Extension (`extension/`, Manifest V3)

- **Popup** — Today/Week toggle, Ala Carte/Program selector; displays categories with English primary, Thai secondary
- **Options page** — Backend URL input; auto-detects and locks field when `MENU_API_URL` is set via managed storage policy
- **`background.js`** — Service worker; seeds `localStorage` with `http://localhost:8000` on install
- **`managed_schema.json`** — Declares `MENU_API_URL` policy key for admin-managed deployments

## README

Full setup guide: local OAuth credentials, service account + sheet sharing, `uvicorn` invocation, loading extension unpacked, example JSON, and spreadsheet format assumptions with TODOs for site-specific tuning.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Build a two-part project for a school lunch menu:
> 
> GOAL
> - Turn a messy Google Sheets spreadsheet (with merged cells and alternating English/Thai rows) into a clean JSON API.
> - A Chrome extension (Manifest V3) will call this API and show today’s menu + the week.
> 
> CONTEXT / SOURCE DATA
> - The source is a Google Sheets spreadsheet.
> - The spreadsheet has multiple tabs; public viewers see two relevant weekly tabs:
>   1) “Lunch Ala Carte”
>   2) “Lunch Program”
> - Each weekly tab name includes a week date range like “(month j - k)”.
> - Inside each tab, the header row (row 1) uses merged cells:
>   - Title is in a merged block (either A1:B1 or A1:C1) containing text like “lunch ala carte” or “lunch program”
>   - Week date range is in another merged block (either C1:F1 or D1:G1) containing text like “2-6 March, 2026”
> - The menu table uses merged regions in column A to indicate category blocks:
>   - e.g. rows 6-15 in column A are merged and contain a category label like “Thai food” (English + Thai in the cell)
>   - Categories can move; do NOT hardcode row numbers.
> - Monday–Friday are columns (typically B–F), but the code should be resilient.
> - Inside each category block, items alternate by row: English row then Thai row, repeating. Pair them into a single item.
> 
> BACKEND (Python FastAPI)
> - Create a FastAPI service with endpoints:
>   - GET /health -> { "ok": true }
>   - GET /menu -> returns normalized JSON for the current week for both menus (ala carte + program)
>   - POST /refresh -> forces re-fetch + re-parse (protect this endpoint with a shared secret header like X-Refresh-Token)
> - Use Google Sheets API to read:
>   - sheet/tab list and properties
>   - merged cell ranges (sheets[].merges) so we can detect header merges and category blocks
>   - values via values.batchGet for computed ranges
> - Authentication:
>   - Support local dev using user OAuth (spreadsheets.readonly scope) storing token locally.
>   - Support production using a service account (ADC) assuming the spreadsheet is shared to the service account email.
> - Implement tab selection:
>   - For each visible tab, read a small header range (A1:G2) and use merges in row 1 to extract title and week range text.
>   - Identify which tab is “ala carte” vs “program” by title text.
>   - Prefer the newest/current week if multiple are present (use week range parsed from tab title or header text).
> - Normalization output schema (example):
>   {
>     "week": { "start": "YYYY-MM-DD", "end": "YYYY-MM-DD", "label": "2-6 March, 2026" },
>     "lastFetched": "...ISO...",
>     "menus": {
>       "alacarte": { "days": { "monday": [ { "category": "...", "items": [ { "en": "...", "th": "..." } ] } ] , ... } },
>       "program":  { "days": { ... } }
>     },
>     "source": { "spreadsheetId": "...", "selectedSheets": [ { "title": "...", "sheetId": 123 } ] }
>   }
> - Parsing rules:
>   - Use merges in column A (col 0) to find category blocks and their row spans dynamically.
>   - For each block, read the adjacent day columns for that row span.
>   - Pair alternating rows into items: (row0=en,row1=th), skip blanks, tolerate odd row counts.
> - Add caching:
>   - Cache parsed JSON in memory with TTL (e.g. 6 hours) to avoid fetching on every request.
>   - /menu returns cached data when fresh; /refresh updates cache.
> - Include logging and clear error messages when parsing fails.
> 
> CHROME EXTENSION (Manifest V3)
> - Create an extension with:
>   - popup UI showing today’s menu and a “This Week” view
>   - option to switch between Ala Carte and Program
> - The extension fetches GET /menu from the backend.
> - Allow configuring the backend base URL via:
>   - a simple options page, AND
>   - chrome.storage.managed policy key (e.g. MENU_API_URL) for admin-managed deployments.
> - Keep UI simple: show categories and items, pairing English/Thai (display English first, Thai smaller or secondary).
> 
> PROJECT STRUCTURE
> - repo/
>   - backend/ (FastAPI app, parsing logic, auth helpers)
>   - extension/ (manifest.json, popup.html/js/css, options page)
>   - README.md with:
>     - local dev setup steps
>     - how to create OAuth client for local dev
>     - how to switch to service account + share sheet
>     - how to run backend locally (uvicorn)
>     - how to load extension unpacked in Chrome
>     - example JSON response
> 
> DELIVERABLE
> - Working scaffolding + clear TODOs where spreadsheet-specific parsing needs to be tuned.
> - Include a small test harness or sample parser unit tests (even if using mocked API responses) to validate merge parsing and row pairing logic.


</details>

author: amazingkivas
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a small, reproducible micro-benchmark to compare OpenMP, Kokkos (different `Layout` / iteration orders) and an explicit SIMD implementation so we can measure whether Kokkos backends inhibit vectorization.
- Give a simple playground to validate layout/iteration choices and to investigate why Kokkos-generated loops may be poorly vectorized.

### Description
- Added a new perf target `vectorization_compare` in `perf-tests/CMakeLists.txt` that builds `vectorization_compare.cpp` and places the binary in `bin/` via `RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY`.
- Implemented `perf-tests/vectorization_compare.cpp`, a minimal memory-bound kernel that measures and prints timings and checksums for: OpenMP baseline (`#pragma omp parallel for`), Kokkos `MDRangePolicy` with `LayoutRight`, Kokkos `MDRangePolicy` with `LayoutLeft` using two iterate orders, and a manual SIMD version using `Kokkos::Experimental::native_simd`.
- Added `perf-tests/README_vectorization.md` with build/run instructions, guidance on interpreting layout/iteration effects, and recommended commands to search Kokkos backend sources and enable compiler vectorization reports for root-cause analysis.
- Kept checksums in each mode to ensure numerical work is equivalent across variants and to make benchmark outputs comparable.

### Testing
- Ran `git diff --check` which passed without issues.
- Attempted to configure the build with `cmake ..` but configuration failed because `KokkosConfig.cmake` was not available in this environment due to submodules not being fetched, so the build could not be completed.
- Attempted to fetch submodules with `git submodule update --init --recursive` but it failed with network/GitHub access errors (`CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`), preventing backend inspection and binary execution.
- No runtime performance runs were executed because Kokkos and submodules were not available in this environment; the README includes exact commands to build and run the benchmark once submodules are present locally.

author: andrewxu313
body:
This PR adds template-level thinking toggle and tool calling support for Kimi K2.5, fixes multi-EOS token handling, and optimizes the MoE decode pipeline with fused kernels and CUDA RMSNorm.

**Stats: 14 files changed, 3,294 insertions, 134 deletions**

---

## 1. Multi-EOS Token Support

Extended EOS handling from single token ID to a set of stop tokens. K2.5 uses both `[EOS]` (163585) and `<|im_end|>` (163586) — the model generates `<|im_end|>` as the chat end-of-turn signal while `[EOS]` is the base vocabulary EOS.

- `eos_token_ids: set` in tokenizer, `batchgen_worker.py`, `decode_task.py`, `decode.py`
- All EOS check sites changed from `== eos_token_id` to `in eos_token_ids`

---

## 2. Thinking Toggle + Tool Calling

Wired chat template features through the batch API so per-request `thinking` and `tools` fields reach the Jinja template:

| Component | Change |
|-----------|--------|
| `io_struct.py` | Added `tools: Optional[List]`, `thinking: Optional[bool]` to `ChatCompletionRequest`; extended `ChatMessage` with `role="tool"`, `tool_call_id`, `tool_calls` |
| `batch_scheduler.py` | Forward `thinking`/`tools` kwargs through `_format_chat_messages()` to `apply_chat_template()` |
| `tokenizer.py` | Implemented `parse_tool_calls()` for K2.5 output format (`functions.func_name:idx` pattern) |
| `tokenizer.py` | Fixed `parse_thinking()` to handle missing opening `<think>` tag (tag is in the prompt, not the decoded output) |

**Thinking toggle**: `thinking=false` in the JSONL body causes the template to emit `<think></think>` (closed empty block), suppressing reasoning. Default (omitted) keeps thinking ON.

**Tool calling**: `tools` list is converted to TypeScript interface format by the upstream tokenizer and injected as a `tool_declare` system message. Model outputs tool calls with `<|tool_call_begin|>functions.name:idx<|tool_call_argument_begin|>{json}<|tool_call_end|>` tokens, parsed into OpenAI-compatible `tool_calls` response objects.

---

## 3. MoE Decode Pipeline Optimizations

Ported optimized kernels and pipeline improvements into the K2.5 decode path:

- **Fused INT4 WGMMA grouped module** (`fused_int4_wgmma_grouped.py`): Inplace operation with TMA descriptor support, processes all persistent experts in 2 kernel launches instead of per-expert launches
- **3D strided dispatch-scatter** (`dispatch_scatter_3d.py`): Fused dispatch and scatter for the EP MoE pipeline
- **CUDA RMSNorm** (`cuda_rmsnorm.py`): Replaced PyTorch RMSNorm with fused CUDA kernels across all 61 layers
- **Triton fused add+RMSNorm** (`triton_add_rmsnorm.py`): Fused residual addition with layer normalization
- **Shared expert on dedicated stream**: Overlaps shared expert computation with AllGather communication

---

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Documentation update

- [x] I have updated the tests (if applicable).
- [x] I have updated the documentation (if applicable).

## Summary

Fix 9 security vulnerabilities and 3 high-priority code quality bugs identified in the security audit.

### Security Fixes
1. **Internal error messages leaked to API clients** (Medium) — Always return generic 500 message
2. **Arbitrary file read via path traversal in install-pack** (High) — Validate relative paths stay within CWD
3. **Pack registry SSRF via custom registryUrl** (Medium) — Enforce https and block private IPs
4. **Connector config path traversal via name** (Medium) — Validate name matches `/^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/`
5. **Rate limiter trusts spoofable X-Forwarded-For** (Medium) — Use `req.socket.remoteAddress` directly
6. **Ollama LLM provider leaks error response bodies** (Medium) — Return generic status-based messages
7. **Web UI server lacks rate limiting** (Low) — Apply `checkRateLimit` middleware
8. **Obsidian vault no path boundary check** (Low) — Verify resolved embed paths stay within vault
9. **SQL string interpolation comment** (Low) — Document why interpolation is safe

### Quality Bug Fixes
10. **`disconnectSlack` FTS5 deletion bug** — Use rowid-based subquery, add try/catch and embeddings cleanup
11. **`deleteConnectorDocuments` same FTS5 bug** — Same fix pattern
12. **Dashboard XSS via document ID** — Use data attributes and event delegation instead of inline onclick

### Tests
- Added security validation tests for path traversal, SSRF, and connector name validation

author: hellblazer
body:
## Summary

Two bugs caught during live validation of rc8.

**Bug 1 — `chroma run --log-level` removed in chroma 1.x**
- `start_t1_server()` passed `--log-level ERROR` to `chroma run`
- chroma 1.3.1 doesn't accept this flag → exits with code 2 immediately
- Session hook caught the early exit and fell back to EphemeralClient
- Fix: remove the flag; stdout/stderr already discarded via DEVNULL

**Bug 2 — Session file keyed to transient shell subprocess**
- `session_start()` called `ppid = os.getppid()` — returns the transient zsh Claude spawns per Bash hook invocation
- That shell dies as soon as the hook exits; subsequent `nx scratch put` calls run in a new shell with a new PPID chain that never intersects the dead shell's PID
- Fix: `ppid = _ppid_of(os.getppid()) or os.getppid()` — grandparent is Claude Code's stable PID, which appears in all Bash subprocess PPID chains for the session
- Verified: `nx scratch put` → `nx scratch list` now returns the stored entry across separate Bash invocations

## Verification
```
nx hook session-start  # writes ~/.config/nexus/sessions/40496.session (claude PID)
nx scratch put "test"  # Stored: <id>
nx scratch list        # [<id>] - test    ← cross-process T1 confirmed
```

### Motivation
- Household share links failed for recipients because newly-created `CKShare` objects did not set `publicPermission`, preventing link-based join and CRUD access.
- The share metadata also needed to be persisted back to CloudKit in the correct (private) store so link recipients gain the intended permissions.

### Description
- In `CloudSharing.fetchOrCreateShare(...)` set `share[CKShare.SystemFieldKey.title]`, set `share.publicPermission = .readWrite`, add temporary debug prints, resolve the private `NSPersistentStore` by locating the `persistentStoreDescription` with `cloudKitContainerOptions.databaseScope == .private` and using its `.url` with `persistentStoreCoordinator.persistentStore(for:)`, then call `persistentContainer.persistUpdatedShare(share, in: store, ...)` and return the persisted `CKShare`.
- In `CloudKitHouseholdSharingSheet.prepareShare(...)` apply the same `publicPermission = .readWrite` assignment, debug logging, private-store resolution via URL, and call `persistUpdatedShare` before invoking the prepare completion handler.
- Kept existing permanent-ID and save logic intact, left the share-acceptance flow unchanged, and relied on the existing `NotificationCenter.default.post(name: .didAcceptCloudKitShare, object: nil)` behavior.

author: haud
body:
## Summary
- Adds a Python script (`draft-assistant/scripts/enrich_positions.py`) that fetches player position eligibility from the ESPN Fantasy API and enriches Razzball projection CSVs with granular, multi-position data
- Replaces generic positions (e.g., `OF` → `LF/CF`, `SS` → `SS/3B`) and detects two-way players
- Includes 54 unit tests covering name normalization, position extraction, player matching, CSV processing, and edge cases
- Stdlib-only — no pip dependencies required

## Details

The Razzball CSVs use coarse positions that don't reflect ESPN's granular eligibility system. This script:

1. **Fetches** all ~1,300 MLB players from ESPN's fantasy API with pagination
2. **Matches** CSV players to ESPN data via normalized name matching (accent-stripping, suffix removal, fuzzy matching with team disambiguation)
3. **Extracts** concrete positions from `eligibleSlots`, filtering out meta-slots (OF, MI, CI, UTIL, P, BE, IL)
4. **Updates** the `ESPN` column in `hitters.csv` and `POS` column in `pitchers.csv` with slash-delimited multi-position strings
5. **Reports** all changes, unmatched players, and two-way player detections

No Rust code changes needed — the ESPN column in CSVs is informational only; position eligibility in the Rust codebase flows through the Firefox extension WebSocket path.

## Test plan
- [x] 54 unit tests pass (`python3 -m unittest scripts/test_enrich_positions -v`)
- [ ] Run against real CSVs with ESPN credentials and review output report
- [ ] Spot-check ~20 enriched players against ESPN website

author: seriouslyawesome
body:
## Summary

Full framework upgrade from **Rails 4.2 / Ruby 2.2** to **Rails 7.2 / Ruby 3.2**, following the path 4.2 → 5.2 → 6.1 → 7.2. Replaces abandoned gems, converts all CoffeeScript to vanilla JS, and gets the test suite passing (157 examples, 0 failures).

### Highlights

- **Rails 4.2 → 7.2**, **Ruby 2.2.7 → 3.2.6**
- **Replaced `activerecord-reputation-system`** (abandoned) with a custom `Vote` model and `Votable` concern
- **Converted all 16 CoffeeScript files** to vanilla JavaScript
- **Replaced Handlebars templates** with JS template literal functions
- **Replaced ~30 deprecated Bourbon/Neat/Bitters SCSS mixins** with plain CSS equivalents
- **Unicorn → Puma** as the application server
- **FactoryGirl → FactoryBot**, updated all spec syntax for RSpec 6+
- **Headless Chrome** replaces older Selenium config for JS feature specs

### Gems removed
`activerecord-reputation-system`, `socialization`, `devise_marketable`, `will_paginate`, `unicorn`, `coffee-rails`, `handlebars_assets`, `quiet_assets`, `rails_12factor`, `heroku_rails_deflate`, `yui-compressor`, `sinatra` (Sidekiq Web UI dep), `codeclimate-test-reporter`

### Gems added
`puma`, `bootsnap`, `responders`, `sprockets-rails`, `terser`, `omniauth-rails_csrf_protection`, `rails-controller-testing`, `database_cleaner-active_record`, `vcr`

### Breaking changes addressed
- `belongs_to` required by default (Rails 5+) — added `optional: true` where appropriate
- `content_tag_for` removed (Rails 5.1) — replaced with `content_tag` + `dom_id`/`dom_class`
- CarrierWave 3.0 removed `MimeTypes` module, changed version object API
- Font Awesome 6 changed icon helper API and renamed icons (`trash-o` → `trash`, etc.)
- Devise 4.9 `http_authenticatable_on_xhr` bypasses `warden.authenticate\!` recall for XHR
- `rails-ujs` fires native CustomEvents; jQuery wraps these so `detail` lives at `e.originalEvent.detail`
- jquery-ui-rails 8.0 changed asset paths (`jquery-ui/draggable` → `jquery-ui/widgets/draggable`)

### Test suite
- **157 examples, 0 failures, 3 pending**
- 2 pending: pre-existing "External API Changes" skips
- 1 pending: flaky jQuery fileupload timing test with headless Chrome

author: beshkenadze
body:
## Summary

Extracts a shared ECAPA-TDNN embedding backbone into `mlx_audio/codec/models/ecapa_tdnn/` and migrates the LID consumer to use it. This is the first step toward consolidating the 4 independent ECAPA-TDNN implementations in the codebase.

Closes #531

## What changed

- **New shared backbone** (`mlx_audio/codec/models/ecapa_tdnn/`):
  - `EcapaTdnnConfig` — dataclass with defaults matching SpeechBrain/VoxLingua107
  - Building blocks: `TDNNBlock`, `Res2NetBlock`, `SEBlock`, `SERes2NetBlock`
  - `AttentiveStatisticsPooling` with `global_context` support (covers all 4 consumers)
  - `EcapaTdnnBackbone` — `(B, T, n_mels)` → `(B, embed_dim)`, NLC format (MLX-native)
- **LID migration**: `EcapaTdnn` now composes `EcapaTdnnBackbone` instead of duplicating the architecture. Classifier and `sanitize()` remain LID-specific.
- **Registered in codec API**: `from mlx_audio.codec import EcapaTdnnBackbone`
- **26 new backbone tests** + all 42 existing LID tests pass (68 total)

## Design decisions

1. **NLC format** — MLX-native Conv1d convention, no transposes
2. **No `return_latent`** — consumers compose sub-modules directly
3. **No `mask` parameter** — YAGNI, no consumer passes one
4. **Hardcode ASTP** with `global_context: bool` — covers all 4 use cases
5. **Per-consumer sanitize** — each loads from different checkpoint format
6. **No classifier in backbone** — task-specific heads stay in domain modules

## Scope

This PR only migrates LID as proof of concept. Spark, IndexTTS, and Qwen3-TTS migration is deferred to follow-up PRs after approval of the shared interface.

## Tests

```
68 passed — mlx_audio/codec/tests/test_ecapa_backbone.py (26) + mlx_audio/lid/tests/test_lid.py (42)
```

author: r33drichards
body:
## Summary

Refactor the fetch and console modules to use V8's cppgc (Oilpan garbage collector) for managing native object lifetimes instead of JSON serialization round-trips and OpState storage. This improves performance and memory efficiency by eliminating unnecessary serialization overhead and leveraging V8's built-in garbage collection.

## Key Changes

**Fetch Module (`server/src/engine/fetch.rs`)**
- Introduced `FetchResponse` struct as a cppgc-managed object holding HTTP response data (status, headers, body, etc.)
- Changed `op_fetch` to return a cppgc-managed `FetchResponse` instead of a JSON string
- Added dedicated accessor ops (`op_fetch_status`, `op_fetch_ok`, `op_fetch_redirected`, `op_fetch_status_text`, `op_fetch_url`, `op_fetch_headers`, `op_fetch_body`) that extract fields on demand without serialization
- Updated JavaScript wrapper to call accessor ops instead of parsing JSON, using getter properties for lazy evaluation
- Implemented `GarbageCollected` trait for `FetchResponse` with proper `Send`/`Sync` safety markers

**Console Module (`server/src/engine/console.rs`)**
- Renamed `ConsoleLogState` to `ConsoleWriter` and made it cppgc-managed
- Added `op_console_init` to create the writer once during JS initialization
- Changed `op_console_write` to accept a cppgc writer handle instead of accessing OpState
- Updated JavaScript wrapper to initialize the writer via `op_console_init` and store it in a closure and `globalThis.__console_writer`
- Refactored `flush_console` and `flush_console_snapshot` to retrieve the writer from the global object via V8 API instead of OpState

**Engine Module (`server/src/engine/mod.rs`)**
- Updated `initialize_v8()` to explicitly call `JsRuntime::init_platform(None)` for consistent platform initialization
- Modified `create_params_with_heap_limit()` to create and attach a cppgc `CppHeap` to the V8 `CreateParams`
- Changed OpState initialization to store the raw `sled::Tree` instead of `ConsoleLogState`
- Added safety check in `execute_stateful` to only snapshot on successful execution, avoiding segfaults when snapshotting a terminated isolate with an attached CppHeap

## Implementation Details

- Both `FetchResponse` and `ConsoleWriter` implement `GarbageCollected` with empty trace methods (no pointers to other GC objects)
- Safety is ensured by marking both types as `Send + Sync` since they're only accessed from the single V8 thread
- The cppgc objects are created on background tasks (fetch) or during initialization (console) but moved to V8's GC heap before JS code accesses them
- Accessor ops use fast paths (`#[op2(fast)]`) for simple returns and standard ops for string returns
- The JavaScript wrapper uses getter properties to lazily call accessor ops, maintaining API compatibility while avoiding upfront serialization

## Summary

Adds **trail strength** — a stigmergic coordination signal for the ForgeStore — enabling ant-colony-style indirect coordination between Koi agents.

- Adds `trailStrength` field to `BrickArtifactBase` and `BrickUpdate` (L0)
- Adds `TrailConfig`, `DEFAULT_TRAIL_CONFIG`, `DEFAULT_TRAIL_STRENGTH` types and constants (L0)
- Adds `computeEffectiveTrailStrength()`, `computeTrailReinforcement()`, `isTrailEvaporated()` pure functions (L0u)
- Extends `sortBricks()` with `orderBy: "trailStrength"` and `minTrailStrength` filtering (L0u)
- Extracts `createMemoryStoreChangeNotifier()` to @koi/validation for cross-L2 reuse (DRY)
- Piggybacks trail reinforcement on `recordBrickUsage()` in @koi/forge (L2)
- Adds `trail_strength` column via SQLite V3 migration (L2)
- Extends fs-store metadata index with trail strength (L2)
- Adds architecture documentation in `docs/architecture/stigmergy.md`

### Key design decisions
- **Separate from fitness**: trail strength measures collective interest (stigmergic), fitness measures individual quality
- **Lazy decay**: exponential decay computed at query/sort time, no background timers
- **MMAS bounds** [0.01, 0.95]: prevents permanent dominance or invisibility
- **Half-life**: 7 days (configurable) for natural evaporation

Closes #254

body:
## Summary

This PR adds a comprehensive gap analysis audit (CCA-1.2) to the audit documentation, identifying 10 findings that were not covered by the previous CCA-1.0 and CCA-1.1 audits. These include compound vulnerabilities (where two separate findings combine into a higher-severity issue), net-new HTTP-layer gaps, and operational blind spots.

## Key Changes

- **Added CCA-1.2 audit entry** to the audit registry table with date 2026-03-01 and description of compound vulnerabilities and HTTP-layer gaps
- **Added appendix reference** to the table of contents linking to the new gap analysis section
- **Documented 10 findings** across security, operational, and infrastructure categories:
  - **GAP-001 (High)**: PIN authentication brute-forceable due to missing rate limiting (compound vulnerability connecting NET-002 + AUTH-002)
  - **GAP-002 (Medium)**: No request body size limits on 15 POST endpoints, enabling memory exhaustion attacks
  - **GAP-003 (Low-Medium)**: Missing Content-Type validation on POST routes
  - **GAP-004 (Medium)**: Unvalidated JSON.parse on scraped external HTML content
  - **GAP-005 (Low)**: No robots.txt allowing search engines to index destructive endpoints like `/db-setup`
  - **GAP-006 (Low)**: No Subresource Integrity (SRI) on external Google Fonts CDN
  - **GAP-007 (Low)**: Source maps not explicitly disabled in production config
  - **GAP-008 (Low)**: No idempotency protection on write endpoints
  - **GAP-009 (Medium)**: `db:push` command runs against production without safeguards, risking data loss
  - **GAP-010 (Info)**: No graceful shutdown handler (non-issue on Vercel, but risk if migrating)

## Notable Details

- Each finding includes severity rating, CVSS score, cross-references to previous audit findings, and specific code locations
- Compound findings explicitly connect previously separate audit items to show how their combination creates higher-severity vulnerabilities
- Recommendations provided for each finding with code examples where applicable
- Summary scorecard shows 1 High, 3 Medium, 1 Low-Medium, 4 Low, and 1 Info finding
- Highlights GAP-001 (PIN brute-force) and GAP-009 (db:push footgun) as highest priority items

author: copilot
body:
`MudAlert`'s `ContentAlignment` parameter had no effect on mobile screens — content always rendered left-aligned regardless of the specified alignment.

## Root cause
`ClassPosition` emitted `justify-sm-*` classes, which Bootstrap-style breakpoint utilities only activate at `≥sm` (600px). At `xs` (mobile), no `justify-content` class was applied, so the flexbox default (`flex-start`) took over.

## Fix
- Changed the generated class prefix from `justify-sm-` → `justify-` so alignment applies at all breakpoints including `xs`

```csharp
// Before
protected string ClassPosition => new CssBuilder("mud-alert-position")
    .AddClass($"justify-sm-{ConvertHorizontalAlignment(ContentAlignment).ToStringFast(true)}")
    .Build();

// After
protected string ClassPosition => new CssBuilder("mud-alert-position")
    .AddClass($"justify-{ConvertHorizontalAlignment(ContentAlignment).ToStringFast(true)}")
    .Build();
```

## Summary

- **Phase 3** (`python/scripts/embed_concept_nodes.py`): Batch-embeds 538 concept nodes across 33 NL database collections using Jina V4 (2048d). Idempotent, verified with full coverage check.
- **Phase 4** (`python/training/rgcn_model.py`, `compliance_predictor.py`, `docs/graphsage-architecture.md`): RGCN link-prediction architecture for predicting compliance edges between code files and code smells. Forward pass verified on dummy HeteroData.
- Phase 5 (export script + training harness) will be added to this branch in subsequent commits.

## Architecture (Phase 4)

- `HeteroRGCN`: Per-type Linear(2048→256) projection + 2-layer RGCNConv with basis decomposition (B=4) + LayerNorm/ReLU/Dropout
- `CompliancePredictor`: MLP link-prediction head (concat src+dst → 512→256→1) + BCE loss with pos_weight=5.0 for 1:5 negative ratio
- Prediction target: `nl_smell_compliance_edges` (106 positive edges, 88/9/9 train/val/test split)
- Full-graph training (no NeighborSampler needed — ~1000 nodes fit trivially in GPU memory)

author: cjimti
body:
## Summary

- **Custom resources**: operators can now define arbitrary static MCP resources in YAML config — brand assets, operational limits, environment docs, or any structured blob that LLMs and agents can read by URI
- **SDK bump**: upgrades `go-sdk` from v1.3.1 to v1.4.0 (no breaking changes; all three txn2 toolkit deps compile cleanly via MVS)

## Custom Resources

### How it works

Extend `resources.custom` with one or more `CustomResourceDef` entries. Each entry is registered as a named MCP resource visible in `resources/list` and readable via `resources/read`. Registration happens at startup, independent of `resources.enabled` (which gates only the dynamic schema/glossary/availability templates).

```yaml
resources:
  custom:
    - uri: "brand://theme"
      name: "Brand Theme"
      description: "Primary brand colors and site URL"
      mime_type: "application/json"
      content: |
        {
          "colors": {"primary": "#FF6B35", "secondary": "#004E89"},
          "url": "https://example.com"
        }

    - uri: "brand://logo"
      name: "Brand Logo SVG"
      mime_type: "image/svg+xml"
      content_file: "/etc/platform/logo.svg"
```

- `content` — inline text/JSON/SVG/anything; set at config parse time
- `content_file` — absolute path; **read on every `resources/read` request** (hot-reload without restart)
- `content` and `content_file` are mutually exclusive
- Invalid entries (missing `uri`, `name`, or `mime_type`; both or neither content fields) are skipped with a `slog.Warn` at startup; valid entries in the same list are still registered

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `pkg/platform/config.go` | `CustomResourceDef` struct; `Custom []CustomResourceDef` field on `ResourcesConfig` |
| `pkg/platform/custom_resources.go` | `registerCustomResources()`, `buildCustomResourceResult()`, `validateCustomResourceDef()` |
| `pkg/platform/platform.go` | Call `registerCustomResources()` in `Start()` after `registerHintsResource()` |
| `configs/platform.yaml` | Commented example `resources.custom` section |
| `docs/server/configuration.md` | New Custom Resources Configuration section |
| `docs/reference/configuration.md` | New Custom Resources Configuration reference table |
| `docs/llms.txt` | Updated configuration index entry |
| `docs/llms-full.txt` | New Custom Resources Configuration section with field table and example |

### Test coverage

11 table-driven tests in `pkg/platform/custom_resources_test.go`:

| Case | Function tested |
|------|----------------|
| Valid inline / valid file | `validateCustomResourceDef` |
| Missing URI / Name / MIMEType | `validateCustomResourceDef` |
| Neither content nor content_file | `validateCustomResourceDef` |
| Both content and content_file | `validateCustomResourceDef` |
| Inline content returned verbatim | `buildCustomResourceResult` |
| File content read and returned | `buildCustomResourceResult` |
| File not found returns wrapped error | `buildCustomResourceResult` |
| Valid defs registered without panic | `registerCustomResources` |
| Invalid def skipped, valid registered | `registerCustomResources` |
| Empty config is a no-op | `registerCustomResources` |

Coverage: `validateCustomResourceDef` 100%, `buildCustomResourceResult` 100%, `registerCustomResources` 85.7% — all above the 80% gate.

## go-sdk v1.4.0

v1.4.0 adds new symbols only — no removed or renamed APIs:

- `CreateMessageWithTools` / `CreateMessageWithToolsHandler` (sampling with tools)
- `SessionMissingError` exported
- `extensions` field in client/server capabilities
- DNS rebinding protection (behaviour, opt-out via `MCPGODEBUG`)
- JSON no-HTML-escaping by default (behaviour, opt-in via `MCPGODEBUG`)

All three txn2 toolkit dependencies (`mcp-datahub v1.0.3`, `mcp-trino v1.0.0`, `mcp-s3 v1.0.0`) pin go-sdk v1.3.1 in their own `go.mod`, but Go MVS selects v1.4.0 for the whole build and they compile without errors. Transitive bumps: `golang.org/x/mod` v0.29.0→v0.32.0, `golang.org/x/sync` v0.18.0→v0.19.0, `golang.org/x/tools` v0.38.0→v0.41.0.

## Test plan

- [ ] `go build ./...` — clean
- [ ] `go test -race ./...` — all pass
- [ ] `golangci-lint run ./...` — no issues
- [ ] Configure a `brand://theme` inline resource, start the server, verify `resources/list` returns it and `resources/read` returns the JSON content
- [ ] Configure a `content_file` resource, update the file without restarting, verify `resources/read` returns the updated content (hot-reload)
- [ ] Configure an entry missing `uri` — verify startup warning logged and entry skipped, other entries still registered

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Contexto (Epic #414 — Tarea 1.9)

Todas las tareas 1.1–1.8 del epic #414 están implementadas y en `main`. La tarea **1.9** es la última pendiente:

> **1.9 Conciliación fiscal (Tesorería vs proyección):** Cada cálculo debe distinguir entre dato estimado (contrato, nómina, etc) y dato real (movimiento punteado Tesorería). Para meses pasados, usar real si existe. Mostrar desviaciones.

### Qué significa en la práctica

Hoy el motor IRPF (`irpfCalculationService.ts`) calcula **todo** a partir de fuentes de proyección:
- **Ingresos alquiler** → `contract.rentaMensual × meses` (estimado)
- **Nómina** → `nominaService.calculateSalary()` (estimado)
- **Gastos OPEX** → `recurringExpensesFiscalService` (estimado)
- **Intereses hipoteca** → `loanInterestService` (estimado)
- **Autónomo** → facturación/gastos estimados

Pero en Tesorería ya existe un sistema de **punteo** (`TreasuryReconciliationView`) donde cada `TreasuryEvent` tiene `status: 'predicted' | 'confirmed' | 'executed'`. Además los registros `Ingreso` tienen `estado: 'previsto' | 'cobrado'` y `movement_id` enlazando al movimiento bancario real. Lo mismo para `Gasto` con `estado: 'completo' | 'incompleto' | 'pagado'` y `movement_id`.

**El objetivo de 1.9** es que para cada partida fiscal, el sistema pueda decir: "el dato estimado es X€, el dato real confirmado en Tesorería es Y€, la desviación es Z€" — y que para meses ya cerrados, el motor use el dato real si existe.

---

## Ficheros clave que debes conocer

### Motor fiscal IRPF actual
- **`src/services/irpfCalculationService.ts`** — Función principal `calcularDeclaracionIRPF(ejercicio)`. Llama a:
  - `recopilarDatosTrabajo()` → lee nóminas activas via `nominaService`
  - `recopilarDatosInmuebles()` → lee contratos, calcula `ingresosIntegros = rentaMensual * meses`, llama a `calculateFiscalSummary()` para gastos/amortización
  - `recopilarDatosAutonomo()` → lee autónomos
  - `recopilarDatosInversiones()` → lee inversiones
- Tipos exportados relevantes: `RendimientoInmueble`, `RendimientosTrabajo`, `RendimientosAutonomo`, `DeclaracionIRPF`

### Resumen fiscal por inmueble
- **`src/services/fiscalSummaryService.ts`** — `calculateFiscalSummary(propertyId, exerciseYear)`: agrega documentos + auto-intereses + gastos recurrentes OPEX por casilla AEAT (box0105–box0117)

### Tesorería — punteo y conciliación existentes
- **`src/components/treasury/TreasuryReconciliationView.tsx`** — UI de punteo mensual. View-model local: `TreasuryEvent { status: 'previsto' | 'confirmado' }`; sumatorios `previsto` vs `real` ya calculados en `globalTotals`.
- **`src/services/db.ts`** — Interfaces:
  - `TreasuryEvent { status: 'predicted' | 'confirmed' | 'executed', actualAmount?, movementId?, sourceType: 'contrato' | 'nomina' | 'prestamo' | 'gasto_recurrente' | ... }`
  - `Ingreso { estado: 'previsto' | 'cobrado', movement_id?, importe, destino: 'inmueble_id', destino_id }`
  - `Gasto { estado: 'completo' | 'incompleto' | 'pagado', movement_id?, total, destino: 'inmueble_id', destino_id }`

- **`src/services/treasuryCreationService.ts`** — `reconcileTreasuryRecord()` marca Ingreso/Gasto como cobrado/pagado y pone `movement_id`
- **`src/modules/horizon/tesoreria/services/treasurySyncService.ts`** — `generateMonthlyForecasts()` crea TreasuryEvents desde contratos, nóminas, préstamos, gastos

### Otros servicios relevantes
- **`src/services/loanInterestService.ts`** — `getInteresesHipotecaByPropertyAndYear()` 
- **`src/services/recurringExpensesFiscalService.ts`** — `getGastosRecurrentesFiscales()`

- **Phase 2**: Migrated all API routes from `:wwn` to `:id`, all handlers use `ResolveDevice()` for backward-compatible lookup, frontend uses `device_id` throughout, Prometheus metrics keyed by `device_id`
- **Phase 3**: Swapped SQLite primary key from WWN to `device_id`, all repository methods query by `device_id` (InfluxDB methods keep WWN), MQTT discovery topics migrated to `device_id`-based identifiers with legacy cleanup, devices without WWN now accepted

## Key changes (64 files, +1047/-522)

### Database
- SQLite PK swap via create-copy-drop-rename migration (SQLite cannot ALTER PK)
- Partial unique index on WWN (`WHERE wwn IS NOT NULL AND wwn != ''`) allows multiple empty-WWN devices
- `RegisterDevice` OnConflict changed from `wwn` to `device_id`
- All 12 SQLite repository methods changed from `WHERE wwn = ?` to `WHERE device_id = ?`
- Added `GetDeviceByWWN()` for backward-compatible resolution

### API & Handlers
- `ResolveDevice()` tries device_id lookup first, falls back to WWN with deprecation warning
- All handler calls use `device.DeviceID` for SQLite methods, `device.WWN` for InfluxDB methods

### MQTT
- Topics use DeviceID (dashes stripped) instead of WWN
- `BuildRemoveMessages` cleans up both new and legacy WWN-based topics
- `LoadInitialData` publishes empty payloads to old WWN topics on startup

### Collector
- Empty WWN is now a warning, not an error
- Removed filter that dropped empty-WWN devices

### Frontend
- All routes and API calls use `device_id`
- Device model includes `device_id` field

- [x] All unit tests pass (reports, deviceid, validation, notify, mqtt, missed ping monitor)
- [x] `go vet` clean (only pre-existing migration tag warnings)

body:
## Phase 1 MC Engine MVP

### GBM Path Simulator (`src/mc/simulator.ts`)
- `simulateBinaryContract()` — crude MC using typed arrays (Float64Array), Box-Muller RNG
- Binary contract: estimates P(S_T > K) under GBM with configurable drift/vol/horizon
- `blackScholesDigital()` — closed-form for validation
- Targets 10K-100K paths, runs well within CF Workers 30s CPU limit

### Variance Reduction (`simulateBinaryContractVR()`)
- **Antithetic variates**: for each Z, also simulate with -Z. Exploits negative correlation in monotonic payoffs.
- **Stratified sampling**: divide U[0,1] into N strata for even distribution coverage. Uses inverse normal CDF (Beasley-Springer-Moro).
- Combined: 50-100x variance reduction so 10K paths ≈ 1M crude paths in precision.

### Brier Score Tracker (`src/mc/brier.ts` + D1 migration)
- `mc_predictions` table: symbol, predicted_prob, strike_price, horizon_ms, outcome, brier_score
- `recordPrediction()` — log MC predictions to D1
- `evaluateExpiredPredictions()` — find expired predictions, fetch actual prices, compute Brier scores
- `getBrierStats()` / `getBrierBySymbol()` — aggregate calibration metrics

### Migration
- `migrations/0004_mc_predictions.sql` — creates table with indices for pending/symbol/created_at lookups

author: copilot
body:
Uploading large files (e.g. 800 MB) failed with an EOF error because the handler buffered the entire request body into a `bytes.Buffer` before calling `PutObject`, exhausting memory and causing connection failures.

## Changes

- **Added** `github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/feature/s3/manager` dependency
- **Replaced** the in-memory buffer + `PutObject` pattern in `handleUpload` with `manager.Uploader.Upload`, which streams the multipart part directly to S3 using S3's multipart upload API — no full-file buffering

```go
// Before: entire file read into RAM
var buf bytes.Buffer
io.Copy(&buf, part)
s3Client.PutObject(ctx, &s3.PutObjectInput{Body: bytes.NewReader(buf.Bytes()), ...})

// After: streamed in chunks directly to S3
uploader := manager.NewUploader(s3Client)
uploader.Upload(ctx, &s3.PutObjectInput{Body: part, ...})
```

The `Uploader` is instantiated once per request (outside the per-file loop) and streams data in 5 MB chunks using S3's multipart upload protocol, handling files of arbitrary size without memory pressure.
