body:
## Summary

Fix the release workflow so the version is correctly read from the release event payload.

## Implementation Summary

The `get_version` step was using `${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}` shell expansion to extract the tag version, but `GITHUB_REF` was empty in the shell environment for the `release: created` event trigger. This caused all downstream steps to receive an empty version string, and `gh release upload ""` to fail with "release not found".

The fix replaces the shell variable expansion with `${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}`, which is a GitHub Actions expression evaluated before the shell script runs and is reliably populated from the release event payload.

## Testing

- Verified the failing run `22552021920` showed `VERSION=` (empty) confirming the root cause
- The `workflow_dispatch` path is unchanged and still uses `${{ inputs.version }}`
- After merging, trigger the workflow manually with `workflow_dispatch` or re-run against the existing `v0.4.0` release to verify artifacts are uploaded correctly

body:
## Descripción

Se ha implementado el módulo inicial para la gestión de salas de espera (Lobbies). Siguiendo las mejores prácticas de arquitectura, se ha separado la lógica de negocio en una capa de **Servicios**, dejando los **Controladores** encargados únicamente de la gestión de peticiones y respuestas HTTP. Se ha probado su funcionamiento a través de Postman.

### Cambios realizados:

- **Lobby Service:** Creada la lógica para generar códigos únicos de sala, creación de nuevas partidas y búsqueda de salas públicas/privadas. Incluye una simulación de base de datos (`mockDb`) para facilitar el desarrollo inicial.
- **Lobby Controller:** Implementados los _endpoints_ para:
- `POST /lobbies`: Crear una sala.
- `GET /lobbies`: Listar salas públicas (con soporte para búsqueda por nombre).
- `GET /lobbies/:lobbyCode`: Obtener detalles de una sala específica para unirse.

- **Tipado:** Integración con `AuthenticatedRequest` para asegurar que solo usuarios logueados puedan interactuar con las salas.

## Cómo probar (Testing)

1. Asegúrate de tener las dependencias instaladas.
2. Realiza una petición `POST` a `/lobbies` enviando un JSON con `{ "name": "Mi Sala", "maxPlayers": 4, "engine": "Classic", "isPrivate": false }`.
3. Verifica que recibes un código de 4 caracteres y un estado 201.
4. Prueba a buscar la sala creada usando el _endpoint_ `GET /lobbies?search=Mi`.

## Notas adicionales

- El sistema de códigos de sala usa una función auxiliar `generateLobbyCode`.
- Se han incluido validaciones básicas de capacidad de sala (error 403 si la sala está llena).

## Summary

Fixes the Docker daemon being effectively silent after `lerim up`: no activity log, no logfire traces, no useful output from `lerim logs`.

### Root causes found and fixed

- **Daemon maintain never triggered in Docker**: `time.monotonic()` in containers reflects VM uptime, not host uptime. When VM uptime < 60 min, `last_maintain = 0.0` meant the maintain check failed silently. Fixed by initializing to `now - interval`.
- **NULL `repo_path` jobs clogged the queue**: 150+ orphaned jobs with no project match were claimed every cycle and immediately skipped, preventing valid sessions from reaching extraction. Added filter in claim query, guard in enqueue, and migration cleanup.
- **Explorer subagent output validation failures**: `grok-4.1-fast` returns empty responses when forced to produce structured `ExplorerEnvelope` output via PydanticAI's result tool. Switched to plain `str` output. Added graceful fallback on explorer errors.
- **Maintain action path validation**: LLM sometimes returns a list of paths in `source_path`; validation now iterates over list elements instead of treating the repr string as a path.
- **Zero daemon logging**: added per-cycle log lines so `lerim logs` shows sync/maintain activity.
- **Hardcoded `trigger="manual"`** in `run_maintain_once`: now accepts a parameter.

### Verified

- 417 unit tests pass
- Real maintain test: exit code 0, 14 archived, 72 unchanged, $0.09 cost

author: bezpowell
body:
**IMPORTANT: Please do not create a Pull Request adding a new feature without discussing it first.**

The place to discuss new features is the forum: <https://zola.discourse.group/>
If you want to add a new feature, please open a thread there first in the feature requests section.

Sanity check:

* [x] Have you checked to ensure there aren't other open [Pull Requests](https://github.com/getzola/zola/pulls) for the same update/change?

## Code changes
(Delete or ignore this section for documentation changes)

* [x] Are you doing the PR on the `next` branch?

If the change is a new feature or adding to/changing an existing one:

* [ ] Have you created/updated the relevant documentation page(s)?

This draft pr is an alternative implementation of perceptual image compression to [#3113](https://github.com/getzola/zola/pull/3113). Instead of adding perceptual compression as a post-processing step as the previous pr does, this incorporates it directly into the `process_image` function.

### How it works?
A new `image_encoders` section is added to the site config. This allows configuration minimum and maximum quality values per image format, as well as the number of binary search 'iterations' to make when doing perceptual compression:
```
[image_encoders]
jpeg = { min_quality = 30, max_quality = 95 }
webp = { min_quality = 20, encode_iterations = 4 }
```
This global encoder configuration is then passed to the function performing enqueued image processing functions. When encoding images, a check is made: if there is no global configuration for that format, Zola's default image encoding code is used. Otherwise, if there is a global configuration for the relevant format, that is used to run perceptual image encoding, with the passed quality level used to infer the target DSSIM value.

In the example above, any calls to `process_image` in templates that set `format` to jpeg or webp would use perceptual encoding with the configured min, max, and iterations values. Any calls to `process_image` in templates that set `format` to png or avif, however, would continue to use Zola's existing image encoding (i.e. single pass at the configured quality level).

### Pros of this approach
- Output format and quality can be set on an image by image basis: While global min and max values are set in `config.toml` (to avoid over cluttering `process_image` with multiple new parameters), the target quality can still be configured per image.
- Less duplication: Compressed images are output to the existing `processed_images` folder.
- Ability to preview images: As perceptual compression is done at build-time, users can see the final images when developing the site from `serve`.

### Cons of this approach
- Slower serve: As perceptual compression is run regardless of build command, processing images for serve is considerably slower using this method.
- Identical file hashes: As ImageOp parameters are untouched with this method, the hash of files encoded via the new method is identical to those of the same quality level without the global config. Users wanting to quickly update all images to the new format would currently have to deleted processed_images for the changes to take effect.

## My thoughts
In my opinion, this method of adding support for perceptual image compression if less invasive to Zola's existing code base, and should make it easier for users to add to existing sites (just add a line to `config.toml`, no need to also update any calls to `process_image` to change quality). However, it does substantially slow down image processing, which could be significant for those wishing a quick iteration time using `serve`. Furthermore, as the pr currently stands, perceptually compressed and non-compressed images have identical hashes. This would probably need to be overcome for the feature to be more useful.

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Establishes a merge strategy policy: every commit on `main` must independently pass lint+tests so `git bisect` works reliably. Adds CI enforcement that validates each PR commit individually and directs contributors to squash-merge when commits aren't self-contained.

## Related Issue

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that changes existing behavior)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional change)
- [x] Documentation update
- [x] CI/CD or tooling change

## What Changed

- **`docs/GIT_MERGE_STRATEGY.md`** — new guide: squash vs rebase decision flowchart, `git bisect` primer, good/bad commit sequence examples
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** — added commit quality rules: each commit must be self-contained (code + tests), merge strategy table
- **`.github/instructions/project.instructions.md`** — Golden Rule #6: bisect-safe commits (applies to AI agents too)
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — `commit-lint-test` job iterates every PR commit, runs `npm test` + `pre-commit` lint per commit, fails with squash-merge directive if any commit breaks independently; fixed working-tree cleanup (`git checkout -- .`) before each commit checkout to prevent "local changes would be overwritten" errors caused by hook-generated files (e.g. `jsdoc2md` output)

CI job logic:

```yaml
commit-lint-test:
  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
  steps:
    - # checkout with fetch-depth: 0
    - # install pre-commit once (outside loop)
    - # for each commit: discard hook changes → git checkout → npm ci → npm test + pre-commit
    - # exit 1 if any commit fails → "This PR must use SQUASH AND MERGE"
```

Decision rule:

```text
Does EVERY commit pass lint + tests independently?
  ├── YES → Rebase and Merge
  └── NO  → Squash and Merge
```

## How to Test

1. Open a PR with commits where an early commit adds code without tests — `commit-lint-test` should fail and output squash-merge guidance
2. Open a PR where every commit is self-contained — `commit-lint-test` should pass
3. Verify `docs/GIT_MERGE_STRATEGY.md` renders correctly on GitHub
4. Confirm that PRs with intermediate commits where `docs/CLIENT_API.md` is stale correctly report "squash and merge" rather than crashing with a git working-tree conflict

## Checklist

### Code Quality

- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Functions are small and focused (max 50 lines)
- [x] Error handling is explicit — no silenced errors
- [x] No hardcoded secrets, paths, or magic numbers
- [x] No TODO/FIXME left in production code

### Testing

- [ ] Unit tests added/updated for new logic
- [ ] Integration tests added/updated where applicable
- [ ] Edge cases and error paths are tested
- [x] All tests pass locally
- [ ] Coverage meets project threshold (when tooling is configured)

### Review Readiness

author: jnowat
body:
Root cause of CI failure: `gradle-wrapper.jar` was never committed to the repository. Without this bootstrap JAR, `./gradlew` immediately exits with "Unable to access jarfile gradle-wrapper.jar", aborting the entire Gradle build before a single line of Android code compiles.

Changes:
- src-tauri/gen/android/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar (NEW) Generated with Gradle 8.9 (`gradle wrapper --gradle-version 8.9`). This 44KB bootstrap JAR is the standard file committed in all Android projects — it downloads the actual Gradle distribution on first run and is required for `./gradlew` to work at all.

- .github/workflows/build-android.yml · Replace `actions/setup-java` Gradle cache with the official `gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4` action (caches ~/.gradle properly). · Use single-quoted `targets:` string to avoid YAML `>-` folding introducing a stray space between target names. · Use explicit `--debug` flag for the debug APK build step. · Use `$NDK_VERSION` shell variable instead of `${{ env.NDK_VERSION }}` expression in `run:` blocks for consistency. · Add `chmod +x gradlew` safety step. · Add APK path validation with diagnostic `find` output on failure. · Set Gradle cache to read-only on PRs and read-write on pushes.

- src-tauri/gen/android/app/build.gradle.kts · Add explicit `ndkVersion = "27.2.12479018"` so AGP uses the correct NDK instead of defaulting to whatever is newest on runner.

- src-tauri/tauri.conf.json · Fix `bundle.android.versionCode` 12 → 13 to match build.gradle.kts.

```ts
export async function POST(request: Request): Promise<NextResponse> {
  const sessionOrUnauthorized = await getSessionOrUnauthorized();

  return NextResponse.json({ data: list }, { status: 201 });
}
```

author: pcfreak30
body:
When findConfigFile fails to create a config file at one location
(e.g., permission denied on /etc/lumeweb/portal), it now continues
to try remaining paths instead of immediately returning an error.

This ensures the system gracefully falls back through default config
locations until one succeeds or all fail.

Changes:
- Modified findConfigFile to continue instead of returning error when
  CreateDefaultConfig fails
- Added test case with conditionalMkdirAllFS to verify fallback behavior
- Fixed related tests to match actual plugin directory structure


---

<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
 This pull request modifies the configuration file discovery logic to improve resilience when creating default configuration files.

**Functional Change:**
When the system attempts to create a default configuration file at a specified path (e.g., `/etc/lumeweb/portal`) and encounters a failure (such as permission denied), it now falls back to the next available path in the search list rather than terminating with an error. Previously, any failure during default config creation would immediately return an error, preventing the system from attempting alternative locations.

**Impact:**
This ensures the application can bootstrap successfully even when the primary configuration directory is not writable, by automatically trying secondary locations (such as user home directories or temporary paths) until it finds a writable location or exhausts all options.

**Test Coverage:**
Added specific test cases to verify the fallback behavior when directory creation fails due to permissions, along with updates to existing tests to align with the current configuration directory structure and API signatures.
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

body:
Phantom space deferral means backspacing after a suggestion pick or punctuation removes the last character of the preceding word rather than the pending space. This adds an opt-in setting (default `false`) to commit the space character immediately instead.

## Changes

- **`Settings.java` / `Defaults.kt`** — New pref key `autospace_immediately_commit`, default `false`
- **`SettingsValues.java`** — New `mAutospaceImmediatelyCommit` field wired to prefs
- **`InputLogic.java`** — Two call sites where `SpaceState.PHANTOM` is set now branch on the new flag:
  - After suggestion pick: calls `insertAutomaticSpaceIfOptionsAndTextAllow()` immediately instead of setting phantom state
  - After punctuation (`handleSeparatorEvent`): sets a local flag `insertSpaceAfterPunctuation` and calls `insertAutomaticSpaceIfOptionsAndTextAllow()` after `commitCodePoint()`, preserving commit order
- **`TextCorrectionScreen.kt`** — Setting exposed in the Space section after "No autospace when pressing shift"
- **`strings.xml`** — Title and summary strings for the new preference

## Scope

Only affects the two phantom-space origins called out in the issue (suggestion pick and `mAutospaceAfterPunctuation`). The PHANTOM-preservation path for chained separators (e.g. picking a suggestion then typing a comma) is unaffected — with this setting on, no phantom state is ever set, so that branch is naturally bypassed.

author: vigneshrajsb
body:
## Problem

Build and deploy job logs are permanently lost once k8s Job pods are evicted or TTL-expired (~24h):

- Job history is fetched entirely from live k8s (`getNativeBuildJobs`, `getDeploymentJobs`)
- Logs are streamed from live pods via WebSocket
- When pods disappear the UI renders a broken \`NotFound\` state with no recovery path

## Solution

Add MinIO as an optional in-cluster S3-compatible object store. Logs are archived at job completion time and served back transparently — the UI sees a new \`Archived\` status instead of \`NotFound\`.

## Architecture

\`\`\`
Job completes → archive logs.txt + metadata.json to MinIO
                 └── {namespace}/{jobType}/{serviceName}/{jobName}/

Pod evicted after TTL...

UI requests log stream info → backend returns status='Archived' + archivedLogs text
UI requests job list       → archived jobs merged into live k8s results (deduplicated by jobName)
\`\`\`

## Changes

### New files
| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| \`src/server/lib/objectStore/s3Client.ts\` | S3Client singleton supporting MinIO (forcePathStyle + explicit creds) and AWS S3 (IRSA) |
| \`src/server/services/logArchival.ts\` | LogArchivalService: archiveLogs, getArchivedLogs, listArchivedJobs, ensureBucket |
| \`src/server/services/types/logArchival.ts\` | ArchivedJobMetadata interface |

### Modified files (lifecycle backend)
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| \`src/shared/config.ts\` | Export \`OBJECT_STORE_*\` env vars with safe defaults |
| \`next.config.js\` | Add \`OBJECT_STORE_*\` vars to serverRuntimeConfig; add \`@aws-sdk/client-s3\` to serverComponentsExternalPackages |
| \`src/server/services/types/globalConfig.ts\` | Add \`logArchival?: { enabled: boolean }\` |
| \`src/server/services/types/logStreaming.ts\` | Add \`'Archived'\` status; add \`archivedLogs?\` field |
| \`src/server/lib/nativeBuild/engines.ts\` | Archive build logs after job completes (success + failure paths) |
| \`src/server/lib/nativeHelm/helm.ts\` | Archive deploy logs after job completes |
| \`src/server/lib/kubernetes/getNativeBuildJobs.ts\` | Merge archived build jobs; upgrade live jobs with missing pods to \`source='archived'\`; add \`source\` field to \`BuildJobInfo\` |
| \`src/server/lib/kubernetes/getDeploymentJobs.ts\` | Same pattern for deploy jobs; add \`source\` field to \`DeploymentJobInfo\` |
| \`src/server/services/logStreaming.ts\` | Fall back to archived log lookup when k8s returns NotFound |
| \`src/shared/openApiSpec.ts\` | Add \`'Archived'\` status, \`archivedLogs\` field, \`source\` field to all relevant schemas |
| \`src/server/db/migrations/001_seed.ts\` | Seed \`logArchival\` config row (disabled by default) |
| \`src/pages/api/v1/.../buildLogs.ts\` | Add \`podName\`, \`error\`, \`source\` fields to inline OpenAPI schema |
| \`src/pages/api/v1/.../deployLogs.ts\` | Add \`Pending\` to status enum, add \`source\` field to inline OpenAPI schema |
| \`src/pages/api/v1/.../logs/[jobName].ts\` | Add \`'Archived'\` status and \`archivedLogs\` to inline OpenAPI schema |
| \`helm/environments/local/lifecycle.yaml\` | Add \`OBJECT_STORE_*\` env vars for local dev MinIO |
| \`Tiltfile\` | Deploy MinIO via \`helm_resource\` for local dev |

### Related PRs
- **helm-charts** (released v0.8.0): https://github.com/GoodRxOSS/helm-charts/pull/32 — MinIO subchart, objectStore secret, deployments envFrom wiring
- **lifecycle-ui**: https://github.com/GoodRxOSS/lifecycle-ui/pull/28 — UI archived log rendering

## Key design decisions

**Feature-gated**: all object store calls check \`globalConfig.logArchival?.enabled\`. Seeded as \`false\` — enabling requires an explicit DB update. Deploying the infra (MinIO pod) is safe before enabling the flag.

**Non-blocking**: archival failures are caught and logged as warnings — they never fail the build/deploy flow.

**Deduplication**: merged archived jobs are deduplicated by \`jobName\` against live k8s results, so a completing job never appears twice.

**S3 support**: set \`OBJECT_STORE_TYPE=s3\` to use AWS S3 with IRSA — no credentials in config. Bucket must be pre-provisioned.

## Enabling

1. Deploy MinIO via helm-charts (v0.8.0+) with \`minio.enabled=true\` and \`secrets.objectStore.enabled=true\`
2. Insert into \`global_config\`:
\`\`\`json
{ "logArchival": { "enabled": true } }
\`\`\`

## Test plan
- [x] \`pnpm lint\` passes ✅
- [x] \`pnpm ts-check\` — no new errors (pre-existing errors in scripts/ and engines.ts unrelated to this PR) ✅
- [x] \`pnpm test\` — 951/951 pass ✅
- [x] With \`logArchival.enabled=false\` (default): system behavior identical to before, no object store calls
- [x] With \`logArchival.enabled=true\`: trigger a build, verify \`logs.txt\` + \`metadata.json\` appear in MinIO bucket
- [x] Delete the job pod manually, verify it still appears in the build job list with \`source='archived'\`
- [x] Click the archived job in the UI — logs render via \`staticContent\` (not WebSocket)

author: lavabeard
body:
…ng on load

Root cause: _save_state() replaced the entire channels JSON section with self.metadata. If _load_state() skipped channels because their media files were not found on disk (e.g. different machine, missing mount, moved files), self.metadata stayed empty. Any subsequent settings save (NIC change, auto-start toggle, etc.) would then overwrite the JSON with an empty channels section, permanently erasing all saved channel data.

Fix — merge-on-save strategy:
- Add self._saved_channels (dict): raw JSON channel entries loaded from disk
- Add self._removed_cids (set): channels explicitly removed via remove_channel()
- _load_state(): populate _saved_channels from raw JSON before processing
- _save_state(): build channels section by starting from _saved_channels (all disk entries) and overlaying current self.metadata; exclude _removed_cids This way channels with temporarily-missing files are preserved in the JSON until their files come back, rather than being silently erased on next save
- remove_channel(): add cid to _removed_cids and pop from _saved_channels so intentional removals are correctly excluded from the merged write
- add_channel(): discard cid from _removed_cids so re-added channels save cleanly

Also fix add_channel() default vbitrate from "6M" to "8M" (matches config.py default)

body:
## Description

This PR introduces comprehensive **PowerShell coding standards** and **Pester testing conventions** to the hve-core project and adds **copyright header requirements** to the existing bash instructions. It also standardizes attribution conventions across AI artifact documentation.

### PowerShell Coding Standards

> PowerShell scripting lacked formal coding guidance, leading to inconsistent patterns across the codebase.

Added *powershell.instructions.md* establishing complete scripting standards for `.ps1`, `.psm1`, and `.psd1` files. The instruction covers a 10-section script structure, module patterns, naming conventions, error handling, CI integration via `Write-CIAnnotation`, parameter validation, PSScriptAnalyzer compliance, and copyright headers. Two complete working examples — a script template and a module template — demonstrate the conventions in practice.

### Pester Testing Conventions

> Pester test files lacked dedicated coding guidance, causing inconsistent test structure across `scripts/tests/`.

Added *pester.instructions.md* (245 lines) establishing Pester 5.x testing conventions for `.Tests.ps1` files. The instruction covers test naming and location, file headers (`#Requires`, copyright), SUT imports via `$PSScriptRoot`-relative paths, `Describe`/`Context`/`It` block structure, mocking with `Mock`/`InModuleScope`, assertions, tag conventions, output handling, and a complete annotated example template. Separated from *powershell.instructions.md* to keep each file focused and avoid excessive length.

### Bash Copyright Headers

Updated *bash.instructions.md* with a copyright header section matching the PowerShell format (2-line Microsoft/SPDX-MIT). Corrected the attribution from *microsoft/edge-ai* to *microsoft/hve-core*.

### Attribution Convention

Updated *ai-artifacts-common.md* to standardize attribution: frontmatter `description` field applies to all artifacts, while the blockquote footer is retained only for skill files (*SKILL.md*).

### Collection and Plugin Metadata

Registered the new PowerShell and Pester instructions across collection manifests and plugin outputs. Updated *coding-standards.collection.md*, *coding-standards.collection.yml*, and *hve-core-all.collection.yml* to include PowerShell and Pester in descriptions, tags, and item lists. Updated *marketplace.json* and plugin metadata to reflect the expanded language coverage. Added plugin symlinks for both *coding-standards* and *hve-core-all* plugins.

## Related Issue(s)

Closes #308
Closes #316

## Type of Change

Select all that apply:

**Code & Documentation:**

* [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change fixing an issue)
* [x] New feature (non-breaking change adding functionality)
* [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature causing existing functionality to change)
* [x] Documentation update

**Infrastructure & Configuration:**

* [ ] GitHub Actions workflow
* [ ] Linting configuration (markdown, PowerShell, etc.)
* [ ] Security configuration
* [ ] DevContainer configuration
* [ ] Dependency update

**AI Artifacts:**

* [ ] Reviewed contribution with `prompt-builder` agent and addressed all feedback
* [x] Copilot instructions (`.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`)
* [ ] Copilot prompt (`.github/prompts/*.prompt.md`)
* [ ] Copilot agent (`.github/agents/*.agent.md`)
* [ ] Copilot skill (`.github/skills/*/SKILL.md`)

> **Note for AI Artifact Contributors**:
>
> * **Agents**: Research, indexing/referencing other project (using standard VS Code GitHub Copilot/MCP tools), planning, and general implementation agents likely already exist. Review `.github/agents/` before creating new ones.
> * **Skills**: Must include both bash and PowerShell scripts. See [Skills](../docs/contributing/skills.md).
> * **Model Versions**: Only contributions targeting the **latest Anthropic and OpenAI models** will be accepted. Older model versions (e.g., GPT-3.5, Claude 3) will be rejected.
> * See [Agents Not Accepted](../docs/contributing/custom-agents.md#agents-not-accepted) and [Model Version Requirements](../docs/contributing/ai-artifacts-common.md#model-version-requirements).

**Other:**

* [ ] Script/automation (`.ps1`, `.sh`, `.py`)
* [ ] Other (please describe):

## Sample Prompts (for AI Artifact Contributions)

**User Request:**

"Write a PowerShell script that validates configuration files" or "Create a PowerShell module for log processing." The instructions activate automatically via the `applyTo` glob pattern (`**/*.ps1`, `**/*.psm1`, `**/*.psd1`) when editing PowerShell files. For test files, "Write Pester tests for the log processor module" activates *pester.instructions.md* via the `applyTo` pattern (`**/*.Tests.ps1`).

**Execution Flow:**

1. User creates or edits a `.ps1`, `.psm1`, or `.psd1` file in the workspace.
2. Copilot attaches *powershell.instructions.md* based on the `applyTo` pattern match.
3. Generated code follows the 10-section script structure: copyright header, `#Requires` statements, `using` statements, comment-based help, `[CmdletBinding()]` declaration, parameter block, `begin`/`process`/`end` blocks, and helper functions.
4. Error handling uses `try`/`catch` with `Write-CIAnnotation -Level Error` for CI-aware output.
5. Module files follow the module pattern with proper manifest (`.psd1`) and script module (`.psm1`) conventions.
6. When editing `*.Tests.ps1` files, *pester.instructions.md* activates and guides Pester 5.x test structure, SUT imports, mocking, and assertions.

**Output Artifacts:**

Generated PowerShell scripts contain structured sections following the convention:

```powershell
# Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation.
# Licensed under the MIT License.

#Requires -Version 7.0

<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Brief description of the script purpose.
.DESCRIPTION
    Detailed description of what the script does.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory)]
    [string]$InputPath
)
```

Generated Pester tests follow the convention:

```powershell
# Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation.
# Licensed under the MIT License.

#Requires -Version 7.0
#Requires -Modules @{ ModuleName = 'Pester'; RequiredVersion = '5.7.1' }

Describe 'Function-Name' {
    BeforeAll {
        . "$PSScriptRoot/../../src/Function-Name.ps1"
    }
    Context 'when given valid input' {
        It 'returns expected output' {
            # Arrange, Act, Assert
        }
    }
}
```

**Success Indicators:**

- Generated PowerShell code passes `PSScriptAnalyzer` validation (`npm run lint:ps`).
- Scripts include the 2-line Microsoft/SPDX-MIT copyright header.
- Parameter names use PascalCase; variables use camelCase.
- Error handling follows the `try`/`catch` pattern with `Write-CIAnnotation` for CI output.
- Pester tests follow `Describe`/`Context`/`It` hierarchy with `BeforeAll` SUT imports.
- Test files pass `npm run test:ps` execution.

author: copilot
body:
Auto-generated `copilot-instructions.md` ends up as an untracked/staged file with no guidance to the user. This adds a post-regeneration check that surfaces a warning through the VS Code UI if the file may be picked up by Git.

## Changes

- **`core.py` — `check_gitignore(workspace)`**: New function that inspects `<workspace>/.gitignore` for any entry covering `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (exact path, bare filename, or `.github/` directory). Returns a list of warning strings (empty = clean).

- **`cli.py`**: Calls `check_gitignore` after a successful `regenerate` and emits each warning to stdout prefixed with `Warning: `, making it machine-readable by the extension.

- **`extension.ts`**: Splits Python stdout on the `Warning: ` prefix — info lines surface as `showInformationMessage`, warning lines as `showWarningMessage` (prefix stripped before display).

- **`test_core.py`**: Adds `TestCheckGitignore` (7 cases) covering: missing `.gitignore`, exact-path match, filename-only match, `.github/` directory entry, unrelated entries, comment/blank-line skipping, and surrounding whitespace.

## Behaviour summary

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| `.gitignore` has matching entry | No warning |
| `.gitignore` exists, no matching entry | Warning via `showWarningMessage` |
| No `.gitignore` in workspace | Warning via `showWarningMessage` |

author: copilot
body:
Build fails with `No space left on device` during `repo sync` because the large LVM volume from `maximize-build-space` is mounted at `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` (default), while the actual build runs at `~/workspace/coinos` on the 12GB root partition.

- Mount the build volume where the build actually happens:
  ```yaml
  build-mount-path: /home/runner/workspace
  ```
  `~/workspace/coinos` is under `/home/runner/workspace`, so it now uses the ~50GB volume instead of the 12GB root partition.

- Remove `/opt/hostedtoolcache` during cleanup to reclaim additional root space
- Add `df -h` for the build volume in diagnostics

Implements #1085. Adds a new read-only tool `confluence_get_space_page_tree` that returns a flat, token-efficient representation of all pages in a Confluence space with parent relationships.

As discussed in [MCPs Are Not Like Other APIs](https://blog.fsck.com/2025/10/19/mcps-are-not-like-other-apis/), MCP tools should support progressive disclosure and minimize the calls an agent needs to understand its environment. Currently, mapping a space hierarchy requires recursive `get_page_children` calls — fragile and expensive. This tool gives agents the full picture in one call.

**Response:**
```json
{
  "space_key": "DOC",
  "total_pages": 42,
  "has_more": false,
  "next_start": null,
  "pages": [
    {"id": "12345", "title": "Home", "parent_id": null, "position": 0, "depth": 0},
    {"id": "12346", "title": "Getting Started", "parent_id": "12345", "position": 0, "depth": 1}
  ]
}
```

Fixes #1085

## Changes

- Add `get_space_page_tree()` method to `PagesMixin` — fetches pages with ancestor expansion, builds flat list with `parent_id`/`depth`/`position`, sorts breadth-first
- Add `get_space_page_tree` server tool in `confluence_pages` toolset (read-only)
- Include pagination metadata (`has_more`, `next_start`, `hint`) when results are truncated at limit

author: fergusean
body:
## Summary
Replace Helm's `--merge` flag with a custom `yq`-based merge strategy to properly handle chart versions with build metadata (e.g., `0.1.0+3` vs `0.1.0+4`). Helm's SemVer comparison treats these as identical and silently drops entries, causing data loss.

## Key Changes
- **Install yq** as a dependency in both `update-helm-index.yaml` and `rebuild-helm-index.yaml` workflows
- **Replace `helm repo index --merge`** with a two-step process:
  1. Generate index without merging
  2. Use `yq` to merge entries while preserving all versions, including those differing only in build metadata
- **Implement custom merge logic** that:
  - Preserves all chart entries from both old and new indexes
  - Deduplicates by version while keeping all unique versions
  - Sorts entries by creation date in reverse chronological order
  - Maintains API version and generated timestamp from the newer index

## Implementation Details
The new merge strategy uses `yq` with environment variables to load both indexes and apply a custom merge operation. This ensures that versions like `0.1.0+3` and `0.1.0+4` are both retained in the final index, rather than being treated as duplicates by Helm's SemVer comparison logic.

body:
Replaces the LiveKit-based voice agent with a Vapi-orchestrated discovery interview, adding Google Gemini 2.0 Flash for dynamic follow-up generation when user answers are vague.

## Frontend

- **`components/VapiAgent.tsx`** — New component replacing `LiveKitAgent`. Initializes Vapi from `NEXT_PUBLIC_VAPI_WEB_TOKEN`, manages call state machine (`idle → connecting → connected → speaking/listening → ended`), renders an audio bar visualizer driven by `volume-level` events, and tracks call duration.
- **`components/InterviewPage.tsx`** — Swaps `<LiveKitAgent />` for `<VapiAgent />`.

## Backend API Routes

- **`/api/vapi/create-call`** — Creates a Vapi web call via the Vapi REST API using `VAPI_API_KEY`, returning call credentials to the client.
- **`/api/vapi/assistant-config`** — GET serves Sarah's full `CreateAssistantDTO` config (GPT-4o, OpenAI voice, system prompt covering all four interview pillars). POST accepts a `followUpQuestion` and injects it as an additional system message.
- **`/api/gemini/generate-followup`** — Accepts `previousAnswer` + `currentPillar`, calls Gemini 2.0 Flash to produce a single voice-friendly follow-up question (no special chars), and returns it for Vapi to speak.

```ts
// POST /api/gemini/generate-followup
{ previousAnswer: "I just want to be a better leader", currentPillar: "Focus Area" }
// → { success: true, followUpQuestion: "Could you describe a recent situation where you felt your leadership fell short?" }
```

- **`/api/vapi/generate`** — Fixed broken existing route: replaced unresolved `generateText`/`google` imports with `@google/generative-ai` SDK and added the missing return statement.

## Dependency

- Added `@google/generative-ai` (v0.24.1) — no known advisories.

> ## Full Vapi Integration with Google Gemini for Leadership Development Discovery Interview
> 
> ### Overview
> Replace the existing LiveKit agent implementation with a complete Vapi integration. The system should:
> 
> 1. **VAPI as Primary Orchestrator**: VAPI handles the voice conversation flow, asking predefined discovery interview questions
> 2. **Dynamic Follow-ups with Gemini**: When user answers are vague, Google Gemini generates context-specific follow-up questions
> 3. **Seamless Integration**: Frontend component connects to Vapi, backend manages call orchestration and Gemini integration
> 
> ### Current State
> - `LiveKitAgent.tsx` is currently used in the "AI box" component
> - `NEXT_PUBLIC_VAPI_WEB_TOKEN` is set in `.env.local`
> - Interview role: Leadership Development Consultant named "Sarah"
> 
> ### Required Changes
> 
> #### 1. Replace `components/LiveKitAgent.tsx` with `components/VapiAgent.tsx`
> - Initialize Vapi with `NEXT_PUBLIC_VAPI_WEB_TOKEN`
> - Handle call lifecycle (start, connect, disconnect)
> - Display call state and audio visualization
> - Implement event listeners for:
>   - Call started
>   - Speech detected
>   - Call ended
>   - Errors
> 
> #### 2. Create Backend API Routes
> 
> **`app/api/vapi/create-call/route.ts`**
> - Create a new call instance
> - Initialize with agent configuration
> - Return call credentials
> 
> **`app/api/vapi/assistant-config/route.ts`**
> - Serve agent instructions with interview questions
> - Update with Gemini-generated follow-ups when needed
> 
> **`app/api/gemini/generate-followup/route.ts`**
> - Accept user's previous answer
> - Generate context-specific follow-up questions using Google Gemini
> - Return follow-up questions for VAPI to ask
> 
> #### 3. Agent Configuration
> The agent (Sarah) should:
> - **Initial Role**: Expert Leadership Development Consultant
> - **Interview Pillars**:
>   1. Focus Area: Specific leadership improvement needed
>   2. Organizational Expectations: What company expects
>   3. Logistics: Training availability
>   4. Motivation: Why important now
> 
> - **Operational Rules**:
>   - Be conversational, not robotic
>   - Ask clarifying follow-up questions when vague answers are given
>   - One question at a time
>   - Keep under 10 minutes
>   - Politely redirect rambling
>   - Summarize needs in two sentences at end
>   - Do not offer advice, only gather information
> 
> #### 4. Integration Flow
> ```
> [Frontend] → [Start Call]
>     ↓
> [Vapi] → [Ask Initial Question]
>     ↓
> [User Speaks]
>     ↓
> [Vapi] → [Transcribe & Process]
>     ↓
> [Check if Vague Answer]
>     ↓
> YES → [Call Gemini API] → [Generate Follow-up] → [Return to Vapi] → [Ask Follow-up]
> NO  → [Continue with Next Pillar] → [Ask Next Question]
>     ↓
> [Interview Complete] → [Summarize & Thank]
>     ↓
> [End Call & Store Transcript]
> ```
> 
> #### 5. Environment Variables Required
> ```
> NEXT_PUBLIC_VAPI_WEB_TOKEN=<user's token>
> VAPI_API_KEY=<backend key for creating calls>
> NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_GEMINI_API_KEY=<gemini key>
> GOOGLE_GEMINI_API_KEY=<backend gemini key>
> ```
> 
> #### 6. Key Features to Implement
> - Real-time call state visualization (idle, connecting, speaking, listening)
> - Audio visualization with bar chart
> - Error handling with user-friendly messages
> - Call duration tracking
> - Transcript display (optional)
> - Automatic recording capability
> - Session management
> 
> #### 7. Component Updates
> - Update `components/InterviewPage.tsx` to use new `VapiAgent` instead of `LiveKitAgent`
> - Keep existing video capture for user side
> - Ensure layout compatibility
> 
> ### Technical Stack
> - Frontend: React with TypeScript
> - Backend: Next.js API routes
